sections.name: 前言
sections.content_zh:
前言

我们在温州市规划局工作，工作范围除了市区本身以外，还有县城及建制镇，这就必然要接触乡村。由于出身和职业的缘故，我们对乡土建筑有着一种特殊的感情，因此，所到之处就拍摄了一些照片，勾点草图。当时并没有"物聚于专长"的用意，更没有发表文章、出书的痴想。岂知这些朴素无华的乡土建筑，触之动心，味之无极，于是我们就深入到广大农村去收集。星移斗转，照片和资料越积越多。乡土建筑那种自然清新、纯净朴素的感觉犹如拾薪，日积愈高，终于使我们萌发了出版这本书的念头。

我们是趁出差之隙而主要是利用星期天、假日到农村去做这项工作的，足迹遍布永嘉县芙蓉、苍坡、岩头、坦下、塘湾、渠口、水云、埭头、西岙、花坦、廊下、下日川、岩坦、下烘头、上烘头、枫林、鹤阳、鹤盛、鹤湾、东皋、蓬溪、下岙、中塘、上塘、大元下；平阳县北山、水头、溪南、五十丈、青街、顺溪、南雁；苍南县碗窑、金乡、钱库、蒲城、马站、霞关、炎亭；瑞安市桐溪、城关；乐清市柳市、白象、茗屿、茗东、湖头、高岙、磐石、慎江、黄华、象阳、翁垟、海屿、雁荡、南阁；瓯海县巨溪、永中、茶山、香山；文成县大峃、南田、珊溪；泰顺县彭溪、雅阳、香溪、雪溪、泗溪、三魁、西垟、大安、庵前、庵下、上洪、下洪、筱村、浦口、上武洋、下武洋等一百多个乡村及温州市郊几十个乡村，拍照、访问、调查，还和电视台合作制作过专题片，又请同济大学城规学院路秉杰教授、阮仪三教授指点帮助。路秉杰等教授于1996年暑假率领教师、研究生刘杰、刘磊等及70名93级建筑学专业学生来永嘉、平阳、泰顺对几十幢优秀乡土建筑进行测绘；1997年刘杰、刘磊两位同志再一次来温州深入乡村寻访实测。现在选出100多张照片，并吸收部分实测图介绍给广大读者。本书付印的照片仅仅是温州乡土建筑的片编孤云，而随照片发表的文章，由于没有进行全面系统的研究，可能是一孔之见；更由于水平所限，鄙陋乖谬之见亦在所难免，若能引起大家的兴趣，也就算达到作者的目的了。

照片带给大家的，仅仅是建筑本身，也即仅仅是"纹化"。我们不想以器物为本位进行剖析，而是将建筑放到其生存环境的宏观背景中去研究，通过揭示这些建筑和自然环境、人文关系等有形无形的背景之间的相互关系，敞开一条接近建筑文化本质特征的可行之路。这种"以底说图"的方法，可称之为将艺术创作主体的意境最后完成于艺术欣赏者的顿悟过程之中。

还有两点要说明的是：一、我们对有些照片加了注释，这并不是屋主或当时营造工匠的想法，而是我们的主观评论，目的是想给读者一些审美启发；二、出于同样道理，有些房屋（或局部）我们从不同角度拍摄，并且选入本书。

作者
1999.12
sections.content_en:
Preface

We work at the Wenzhou Urban Planning Bureau, and our work scope includes not only the urban area itself but also county seats and designated towns, which inevitably brings us into contact with villages. Due to our background and profession, we have a special affection for vernacular architecture. Therefore, wherever we went, we took some photos and sketched rough drawings. At that time, we had no intention of "accumulating expertise," let alone the ambition of publishing articles or books. Little did we know that these simple and unadorned vernacular buildings would touch our hearts and offer endless fascination, so we began to go deep into the vast countryside to collect materials. As time passed, photos and materials accumulated more and more. The natural, fresh, pure and simple feeling of vernacular architecture is like gathering firewood—growing day by day—until finally we conceived the idea of publishing this book.

We took advantage of business trips and mainly used Sundays and holidays to do this work, our footprints covering over a hundred villages and dozens of suburban villages in the Wenzhou area: Yongjia County (Furong, Cangpo, Yantou, Tanxia, Tangwan, Qukou, Shuiyun, Daitou, Xi'ao, Huatan, Langxia, Xiari chuan, Yantan, Xiahongtou, Shanghongtou, Fenglin, Heyang, Hesheng, Hewan, Donggao, Pengxi, Xia'ao, Zhongtang, Shangtang, Dayuanxia); Pingyang County (Beishan, Shuitou, Xinan, Wushizhang, Qingjie, Shunxi, Nanyan); Cangnan County (Wanyao, Jinxiang, Qianku, Pucheng, Mazhan, Xiaguan, Yanting); Rui'an City (Tongxi, Chengguan); Yueqing City (Liushi, Baixiang, Mingyu, Mingdong, Hutou, Gao'ao, Panshi, Shenjiang, Huanghua, Xiangyang, Wengyang, Haiyu, Yandang, Nange); Ouhai County (Juxi, Yongzhong, Chashan, Xiangshan); Wencheng County (Daxue, Nantian, Shanxi); Taishun County (Pengxi, Yayang, Xiangxi, Xuexi, Sixi, Sankui, Xiyang, Da'an, Anqian, Anxia, Shanghong, Xiahong, Xiaocun, Pukou, Shangwuyang, Xiawuyang), etc. We took photos, conducted interviews and surveys, collaborated with television stations to produce documentary programs, and also invited Professors Lu Bingjie and Ruan Yisan from the School of Urban Planning and Architecture of Tongji University for guidance and assistance. In the summer of 1996, Professor Lu Bingjie and others led teachers, graduate students Liu Jie, Liu Lei, and 70 architecture students of the class of 1993 to survey dozens of outstanding vernacular buildings in Yongjia, Pingyang, and Taishun; in 1997, comrades Liu Jie and Liu Lei once again came to Wenzhou to conduct in-depth field surveys in villages. We have now selected over 100 photos and incorporated some survey drawings to introduce to readers. The photos printed in this book are merely fragments of Wenzhou's vernacular architecture, and the accompanying articles, lacking comprehensive and systematic research, may represent limited perspectives; moreover, due to our limited level, superficial and erroneous views are inevitable. If this book can arouse readers' interest, it will have achieved the authors' purpose.

What photos bring to everyone is merely the building itself, i.e., merely "patternization." We do not wish to analyze based on artifacts alone, but rather to study architecture within the macro context of its living environment. By revealing the interrelationships between these buildings and their natural environment, human relations, and other tangible and intangible backgrounds, we open a path toward approaching the essential characteristics of architectural culture. This method of "explaining the image through the background" can be described as completing the artistic conception of the creative subject ultimately in the epiphany process of the art appreciator.

Two points need clarification: First, we have added annotations to some photos. These are not the ideas of the homeowners or the craftsmen who built them at the time, but our subjective comments, aimed at providing readers with some aesthetic inspiration; Second, for the same reason, some buildings (or parts thereof) we photographed from different angles and selected for inclusion in this book.

Authors
December 1999

chapters.name: 第一章 温州乡土建筑的生成条件

sections.name: 一、自然条件
sections.content_zh:
一、自然条件

1. 气候

温州位于浙江省南部，濒临东海，地处东经119°32′～121°16′，北纬27°05′～28°37′之间，属亚热带海洋性季风气候，冬季盛行从大陆吹来的西北风，气温较低，雨水较少，湿度较小；夏季盛行从海洋吹来的东南风，湿度大，雨水多，气温较高；春季天气多变，时常阴雨连绵；秋季大气较为稳定，常见"秋高气爽"。其气候总特点是：湿度适中，热量丰富，降水充沛，空气湿润，四季分明，季风显著，气候多样，灾害频繁。其光照、热量、降水三方面的气候特点是：

光照：太阳年辐射总量为184.1kcal/cm²（1kcal = 4.1868×10³J），年日照时数为1830h，年日照百分率为41%。

热量：全年平均气温在16～18℃之间，最热的七月份平均气温在26～29℃之间，极端最高气温为41℃，最冷的一月份平均气温为7～8℃，极端最低气温为-9℃，全年无霜期为260～280天。

降水：多年平均降雨量为1730mm，多年平均蒸发量为1310mm。降水主要集中在4～9月，以梅雨、台风雨为主，梅雨后的七月，晴热少雨，常有旱象；夏秋之交，时受台风侵袭，有时伴有暴雨，易造成灾害性气候。

2. 地形

温州大部分地区是山地和丘陵，土地结构为七山二水一分田。

区内地形为：西北高、南东低，地势由西北向南东倾斜。山脉呈北东向展布，且与海岸线略为斜交，并在北东端伸入东海，形成"里亚斯"式海岸（海岸曲折，海湾岛屿众多），是优良的天然港口。其西北部为中、低山区，南东部为丘陵或滨海型河流三角洲平原区。

其山地或丘陵大多由火山沉积岩构成，部分丘陵为花岗岩，最高山峰往往为流纹岩；而主要河流流向又常与山脉走向垂直或大角度斜交，在流水强烈作用下，地形常被切割得支离破碎，形成著名的"雁荡地貌"，成为旅游胜地。
sections.content_en:
1. Natural Conditions

1. Climate

Wenzhou is located in southern Zhejiang Province, bordering the East China Sea, between 119°32′～121°16′ east longitude and 27°05′～28°37′ north latitude. It has a subtropical maritime monsoon climate. In winter, northwest winds from the continent prevail, with lower temperatures, less rainfall, and lower humidity; in summer, southeast winds from the ocean prevail, with high humidity, abundant rainfall, and higher temperatures; spring weather is changeable, often with continuous rain; autumn atmosphere is relatively stable, commonly known as "clear autumn skies and crisp air." Its overall climatic characteristics are: moderate humidity, abundant heat, sufficient precipitation, humid air, four distinct seasons, significant monsoons, diverse climates, and frequent disasters. Its climatic characteristics in terms of light, heat, and precipitation are:

Light: Total annual solar radiation is 184.1 kcal/cm² (1 kcal = 4.1868×10³J), annual sunshine hours are 1830h, annual sunshine percentage is 41%.

Heat: Annual average temperature is between 16～18℃, the hottest July average temperature is between 26～29℃, extreme maximum temperature is 41℃, the coldest January average temperature is 7～8℃, extreme minimum temperature is -9℃, annual frost-free period is 260～280 days.

Precipitation: Multi-year average rainfall is 1730mm, multi-year average evaporation is 1310mm. Precipitation is mainly concentrated in April～September, dominated by plum rain and typhoon rain; July after the plum rain is hot and dry with little rain, often with drought; at the turn of summer and autumn, it is sometimes hit by typhoons, occasionally accompanied by heavy rain, easily causing disastrous climates.

2. Terrain

Most of Wenzhou is mountainous and hilly, with a land structure of "seven mountains, two waters, one field."

The regional terrain is: high in the northwest, low in the southeast, with terrain sloping from northwest to southeast. Mountains extend in a northeast direction, slightly oblique to the coastline, and extend into the East China Sea at the northeast end, forming a "Rias" type coast (winding coastline, numerous bays and islands), which is an excellent natural harbor. Its northwestern part is medium and low mountainous area, while the southeastern part is hilly or coastal river delta plain area.

Its mountains and hills are mostly composed of volcanic sedimentary rocks, some hills are granite, and the highest peaks are often rhyolite; while the main river flow direction is often perpendicular or at a large oblique angle to the mountain trend. Under the strong action of flowing water, the terrain is often cut into fragments, forming the famous "Yandang landform," which has become a tourist attraction.

sections.name: 二、社会背景
sections.content_zh:
二、社会背景

春秋战国时代，我国东南沿海称作"越"，其中，今天温州、台州一带称"瓯越"。它处于浙北良渚文化与福建昙石山文化交接处。古瓯越人的主要经济活动是渔猎。《山海经·海内南经》说"瓯居海中"，《逸周书·王会解》称"东越海蛤，瓯人蝉蛇"。可见，春秋战国时代，瓯越还很原始，不属于中原文化体系。秦统一天下，属闽中郡，不在中央王朝直接管辖之内。西汉惠帝三年，建东瓯王城。

古代温州，有两个重要发展时期。西晋末年中原大乱，大批中原士族南渡，其中很多人到了温州（时称永嘉），《明嘉靖温州府志》记："永嘉（注：年号）之后，帝室东迁，衣冠避难，多所萃止，艺儒术斯之为盛。"于是给温州经济发展带来转机，人文逐渐兴起。刘宋时成为"控山负海，利兼水陆，东南之沃壤，一郡之巨会"（《永嘉嘉靖府志》）。隋唐代大力兴修水利，开发圩田；到了北宋，温州经济已经相当发达，当时的温州太守杨蟠诗咏温州"一片繁华海上头，从来唤作小杭州"。宋代士族地主消亡，庶族地主兴起，开科取士，平民子弟可藉发奋读书中举而进入仕途，因而提高了整个社会的文化水平。宋王朝采取文化开放政策，因而学术思想比较自由，产生了程朱理学。温州出过不少理学家，后理学受压，温州乡间创办了很多书院，成为传播理学的基地。温州历史上第二个大发展时期是宋室南渡，这里实际上成为京畿之地，一方面是先进的中原文化和经济聚集到这里来，另一方面是自身的发展。当时，中原人文荒落，温州却科名极盛，在北宋有叶适为代表的事功学派——永嘉学派。程朱之学经实践，批判产生了以温州人叶适为代表的事功学说——永嘉学派。南戏也发祥于温州，温州成为当时全国学术思想中心，在经济、文化上都居重要地位。

南宋是温州文化史发展的高峰，经济文化的繁荣必促进建筑业的发展。从各县县志和一些宗谱上可见，宋代温州的乡土建筑已十分繁荣，只是时代久远，那些地面建筑大部分已不复存在，我们今天感觉到的乡土建筑高潮发生在明朝。经济是建筑业发展的首要条件，而建筑风格则和学术思想息息相关，温州历史上，尤其是南宋时期学术思想最为活跃，使建筑界的先进思想、先进技术得以在此流行。如北宋浙东木工喻皓的《木经》的发表，南宋绍兴年间《营造法式》的重刊，明代计成的《园冶》、文震亨的《长物志》、李渔的《闲情偶寄》、李斗的《工段营造录》以及清代的《营造法原》等的问世，无不对温州的建筑发生影响。今天我们所看到的温州建筑，把渊源探源都是这个文化背景下的产物。
sections.content_en:
2. Social Background

During the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods, China's southeast coast was called "Yue," among which the area of today's Wenzhou and Taizhou was called "Ouyue." It was located at the junction of the Liangzhu culture of northern Zhejiang and the Tanshishan culture of Fujian. The main economic activity of the ancient Ouyue people was fishing and hunting. "The Classic of Mountains and Seas · South of the Inner Seas" says "Ou resides in the sea," and "Yi Zhou Shu · Wang Hui Jie" states "Dongyue sea clams, Ou people cicada snakes." It can be seen that during the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods, Ouyue was still very primitive and did not belong to the Central Plains cultural system. After Qin unified the country, it belonged to Minzhong Commandery, not under the direct jurisdiction of the central dynasty. In the third year of Emperor Hui of Western Han, the Dong'ou King City was established.

Ancient Wenzhou had two important development periods. In the late Western Jin Dynasty, the Central Plains was in great turmoil, and a large number of Central Plains aristocratic families crossed south, many of whom came to Wenzhou (then called Yongjia). The "Ming Jiajing Wenzhou Prefecture Annals" records: "After Yongjia (note: era name), the imperial court moved east, nobles took refuge, many gathered here, arts and Confucianism flourished." This brought a turning point to Wenzhou's economic development, and humanities gradually rose. During the Liu Song period, it became "controlling mountains and facing the sea, benefiting from both land and water, fertile land of the southeast, a major metropolis of the commandery" ("Yongjia Jiajing Prefecture Annals"). During the Sui and Tang dynasties, water conservancy was vigorously developed and polder fields reclaimed; by the Northern Song Dynasty, Wenzhou's economy was already quite developed. At that time, Wenzhou's prefect Yang Pan wrote a poem praising Wenzhou as "a prosperous head on the sea, always called little Hangzhou." In the Song Dynasty, aristocratic landlordism declined, commoner landlordism rose, and the imperial examination system was established, allowing commoner children to enter official careers through diligent study and passing examinations, thereby raising the cultural level of the entire society. The Song Dynasty adopted an open cultural policy, so academic thought was relatively free, giving rise to Cheng-Zhu Neo-Confucianism. Wenzhou produced many Neo-Confucian scholars; later, when Neo-Confucianism was suppressed, many academies were founded in Wenzhou's countryside, becoming bases for spreading Neo-Confucianism. The second major development period in Wenzhou's history was the southward move of the Song court; here it actually became the capital region. On the one hand, advanced Central Plains culture and economy gathered here; on the other hand, it developed itself. At that time, while the Central Plains was culturally desolate, Wenzhou had extremely prosperous imperial examination success. In the Northern Song Dynasty, there was the utilitarian school represented by Ye Shi — the Yongjia School. Through practice and critique of Cheng-Zhu learning, the utilitarian doctrine represented by Wenzhou native Ye Shi — the Yongjia School — emerged. Nanxi (southern drama) also originated in Wenzhou, making Wenzhou the national academic and ideological center at that time, occupying an important position in economy and culture.

The Southern Song Dynasty was the peak of Wenzhou's cultural history, and economic and cultural prosperity inevitably promoted the development of architecture. From county annals and some genealogies, it can be seen that vernacular architecture in Wenzhou was already very prosperous during the Song Dynasty, but due to the passage of time, most of those above-ground buildings no longer exist. The vernacular architecture climax we feel today occurred in the Ming Dynasty. Economy is the primary condition for architectural development, while architectural style is closely linked to academic thought. In Wenzhou's history, especially during the Southern Song Dynasty, academic thought was most active, allowing advanced architectural ideas and technologies to prevail here. For example, the publication of "Mu Jing" (Timber Classic) by Yu Hao, a carpenter from eastern Zhejiang in the Northern Song Dynasty; the reprinting of "Yingzao Fashi" (State Building Standards) during the Shaoxing period of the Southern Song Dynasty; the publication of " Yuan Ye" (Garden Treatise) by Ji Cheng, "Chang Wu Zhi" (Treatise on Superfluous Things) by Wen Zhenheng, "Xian Qing Ou Ji" (Casual Notes on Idle Feelings) by Li Yu, "Gong Duan Ying Zao Lu" (Records of Construction Works) by Li Dou in the Ming Dynasty, and "Yingzao Fa Yuan" (Building Method Origins) in the Qing Dynasty — all influenced Wenzhou's architecture. The Wenzhou architecture we see today, when traced to its origins, is a product of this cultural background.

Yuan Ye (Garden Treatise by Ji Cheng)

sections.name: 三、民俗
sections.content_zh:
三、民俗

温州民俗，源远流长，特色鲜明。瓯人在原始渔猎时期有"剪发文身"、"蝉蛇顺食之美"、"且瓯文蜃"（《佚周书·王会解》）等独特的生活习俗。西周春秋时期有石棚墓葬，端午竞龙舟祈赛之俗。其后盛行东瓯王敬鬼，民间巫祀之风。永嘉建郡以后，王羲之守郡"以礼仁导之，而人益知向方"。隋唐流行祀神歌舞，宋代盛行"灯会"。有关明代的风俗，据明代温州人姜准在《岐海琐谈》中记载：

元旦，夙兴，放火爆启门。燃香烛望空而拜，次拜祖考，次及阖家长幼尊卑。外而姻族往来，至初四五方止。

元夕，张灯街及神庙，起十二三至十七八方止。街市结盖松棚，或用欢门。神庙如仁济、忠靖、惠民、广惠诸庙以球囊、竹丝灯等装饰。华灯角胜争奇，游观者肩摩踵接，几无置足之地。村落糊楮象龙首尾，裁版为身，机转辘轳，篝灯于上，从以金鼓沿门索赏，谓之"龙船灯"。

立春，先日迎土牛委县，厢隅里长各行铺户，扮饰优者为诸项故事，乘载抬阁马匹，导以金鼓，间以香亭彩门，自郭外迎入府治，谓曰"迎春"。观者填衢塞道。

清明，折柳于门，携榼放舟，上坟祭扫，挂纸钱于墓，亦有因之拉宾行乐者。

端午，悬蒲艾于门，造角黍黑饭以馈遗亲戚者，以雄黄、菖本泛酒饮之，仍用以沫小儿诸窍，复以色丝为索，名"长命缕"，系其臂足，煎百草为汤，老幼毕浴，社庙备龙舟竞渡，几至浃旬。

六月六日，浣濯什器，沐发，浴猫犬。

七月七日，制米面为各项巧食，除去彩缕。

中元日，祭先或作盂兰盆追荐，街坊好事者延僧道普施孤魂。

中秋夜，办酒肴赏月，贫窭亦然，不因雨阻，倾城男女往双门观潮，亦有掬之以醯面者。

重阳，俱往登高，携觞者罕。

冬至，唯官府拜节，民度则否。制秫米为丸糍祀先。

腊月，选吉扫尘，既望后，随家丰俭，俱备牲醴祀神。谓曰：还冬。仍以皎余互相邀款。

廿四夜，以饴果祭灶或倩黄冠送灶君。人家厅宇及衢巷，燎火放爆，往往皆然。

除夜，易桃符、春贴、沃米为饭菽，以充新正之食。燎火放爆，一同前日。合家长幼拥护团坐。名为"守岁"。诸房室燃烛，名"点岁灯"。造色楮为泉，曳而长之，悬诸楣楹。至若井灶圈圊，俱设纸马。炊粉米为糕糍，侑以果品腥牲，交相馈赠，列香烛、糕果供奉家堂香火，按祖先遗像于家及祠，一如奉神之礼。越新正第五日方除，俗号"拆龙盘"。焚其所挂楮钱，曰"烧年纸"。于是诸色人等各执所业，曰："开年假"。
sections.content_en:
3. Folk Customs

Wenzhou folk customs have a long history and distinctive features. The Ou people in the primitive fishing and hunting period had unique living customs such as "cutting hair and tattooing the body," "the delicacy of cicada and snake food," and "Ou decorated clams" ("Yi Zhou Shu · Wang Hui Jie"). During the Western Zhou and Spring and Autumn periods, there were dolmen burials and the custom of dragon boat racing at Duanwu. Later, the worship of the Dong'ou King and ghosts prevailed, with folk shamanic sacrifice customs. After Yongjia was established as a commandery, Wang Xizhi governed it "guiding with propriety and benevolence, and people increasingly knew the right direction." During the Sui and Tang dynasties, sacrificial singing and dancing were popular, and in the Song Dynasty, "lantern festivals" prevailed. Regarding Ming Dynasty customs, according to records by Wenzhou native Jiang Zhun in "Qi Hai Suo Tan" (Trivial Talks of the Qihai):

New Year's Day: rise early, set off firecrackers and open doors. Light incense and candles and bow toward the sky, then worship ancestors, then the whole family by seniority. External relatives visit each other until the fourth or fifth day.

Lantern Festival (15th of first month): hang lanterns on streets and temples, from the 12th/13th to the 17th/18th. Streets and markets build pine canopies or use festive gates. Temples such as Renji, Zhongjing, Huimin, and Guanghui are decorated with ball pouches and bamboo-silk lanterns. Fancy lanterns compete in beauty, with visitors shoulder to shoulder, barely room to stand. Villages paste paper into dragon head and tail shapes, cut boards for the body, with rotating pulleys and lanterns on top, accompanied by gongs and drums going door to door seeking rewards, called "dragon boat lanterns."

Start of Spring: the day before, welcome the clay ox to the county; neighborhood heads and shop owners dress performers as various story characters, carried on sedan chairs and horses, led by gongs and drums, interspersed with incense pavilions and colorful gates, welcomed from outside the city into the prefectural government, called "welcoming spring." Spectators fill the streets.

Qingming: break willow branches at doors, carry wine containers on boats, visit graves for sweeping and sacrifices, hang paper money at graves, some also invite guests for pleasure.

Duanwu: hang calamus and mugwort at doors, make zongzi and black rice to give to relatives, drink wine with realgar and calamus, also use it to touch children's orifices, use colored silk as cords called "longevity threads" tied to arms and feet, boil all kinds of herbs for bathing, old and young all bathe; community temples prepare dragon boat races, lasting nearly ten days.

Sixth day of sixth month: wash utensils, wash hair, bathe cats and dogs.

Seventh day of seventh month: make rice flour into various fancy foods, remove colored threads.

Zhongyuan (Ghost Festival): worship ancestors or hold Ullambana services for the dead; neighborhood enthusiasts invite monks and Taoist priests to universally give to wandering souls.

Mid-Autumn night: prepare wine and food to admire the moon, even the poor do so, not stopped by rain; the whole city's men and women go to Shuangmen to watch the tide, some also collect it with vinegar and flour.

Chongyang: all go climbing, few carry wine.

Winter Solstice: only government offices exchange greetings, common people do not. Make glutinous rice balls and cakes to worship ancestors.

Twelfth month: choose an auspicious day to dust; after the full moon, according to family wealth, all prepare meat and wine to worship gods, called "returning winter." Still use leftovers to invite each other.

24th night: worship the stove god with candy and fruit or ask Taoist priests to send off the stove god. In halls and alleys, people light fires and set off firecrackers, often so.

New Year's Eve: change peachwood charms and spring couplets, soak rice for New Year food. Light fires and firecrackers, same as before. The whole family, old and young, sit together, called "keeping the year." All rooms light candles, called "lighting year lamps." Make colored paper into money, stretched long, hung on lintels and pillars. Even wells, stoves, pigsties, and latrines all have paper horses. Steam rice flour into cakes, accompanied by fruit and meat, exchanged as gifts; arrange incense, candles, cakes, and fruit to worship family shrine spirits, place ancestor portraits at home and in ancestral halls, just like worshipping gods. Removed only on the fifth day of the new year, commonly called "dismantling the dragon coil." Burn the hung paper money, called "burning year paper." Then all tradespeople resume their work, called "ending New Year holiday."

chapters.name: 第二章 温州乡土建筑的地方特色

sections.name: 一、不甚理性，注重实际
sections.content_zh:
一、不甚理性，注重实际

"温州好，别自一乾坤，宜雨宜晴天较远，不寒不燠气恒温，风色异朝昏"，这是清代温州外籍朝庭命官孙扩图描写温州风土人情的一系列竹枝词之一。该词正确地把握了温州的气候特色。犹如这细腻多变的气候，温州的生活方式也丰富而多彩。建筑与之同构，温州乡土建筑的整体特征是丰富细腻的。

本节所说温州乡土建筑的地方特色，主要是指住宅而言，《黄帝宅经》说："宅者，人之本。人以宅为家，居若安，即家代昌吉，……"，所以历来家家都注重住宅营造，成为乡土建筑的主体，亦是决定村落面貌的最重要因素。乡土公共建筑将另立章节研究。

如第一章所述，温州气候闷热，多山多水多台风，风俗总体特征为巫风；地形封闭，有康有为先生称之为"截"（即三面环山，一面向海）的特征；同时，它与内地联系不便，而与海外交往盛行。温州的祖先长期和这些要素打交道，长期在这样的模式中生产、生活，形成了不重理论、注重实际、敢于开拓的性格和亲近山水的文化、心理图式。作为多元文化现象的建筑，与文化、心理图式同构，不甚理性，而注重实际。和其他地区民居比较，徽州民居、山西大户民居最具"儒气"、"商气"，江南水乡民居最具"文气"和"灵气"，而温州民居则介于"儒气"、"野气"之间。

"儒气"重的民居其根源是受方形田制、方形城制以及理性、礼制约束，因此，形成了以轴对称、纵深发展、内省气质强、天井式为主要特征的方形宅制。温州民居不甚理性，注重实际，创作目的讲究实用，创作方法采用了与背景"适形"的造物原则，形成了开放式的"一"字形形制。从村落、住宅的选址、布局角度看，温州多山，山区里田地零碎分散，人们为了尽量腾出耕地，而使自己的居屋尽量贴近山，跟山走、跟水走、跟地形走，所以，有很多的房子、村落表现出来的气质如行云流水，仿佛是从环境中长出来一样，可用"屋宇同位，三理（天理、地理、生理）合一"八个字概括其文化底蕴。
sections.content_en:
1. Less Rational, Pragmatic

"Wenzhou is fine, a world of its own; rainy or sunny the sky seems far, neither cold nor hot the air is always mild, the wind changes with dawn and dusk" — this is one of a series of zhuzhi ci (bamboo branch poems) by Sun Kuo tu, a non-native official in Wenzhou during the Qing Dynasty, describing Wenzhou's local customs and people. The poem correctly captures Wenzhou's climatic characteristics. Just like this delicate and changeable climate, Wenzhou's way of life is also rich and colorful. Architecture is isomorphic with it, and the overall characteristic of Wenzhou vernacular architecture is rich and delicate.

The local characteristics of Wenzhou vernacular architecture discussed in this section mainly refer to residences. The "Yellow Emperor's House Classic" says: "A house is the foundation of people. People take a house as home; if living is peaceful, the family will prosper for generations..." Therefore, historically every family has focused on house construction, making residences the main body of vernacular architecture and the most important factor determining the appearance of villages. Vernacular public buildings will be studied in a separate chapter.

As described in Chapter 1, Wenzhou has a hot and humid climate, many mountains, waters, and typhoons; the overall characteristic of customs is shamanistic; the terrain is enclosed, described by Kang Youwei as "cut off" (i.e., surrounded by mountains on three sides, facing the sea on one side); at the same time, it has inconvenient connections with the interior but盛行 overseas exchanges. Wenzhou's ancestors long interacted with these elements, producing and living in this mode for a long time, forming a personality that values practice over theory, is pragmatic and pioneering, and a cultural and psychological schema close to mountains and waters. As a multicultural phenomenon, architecture is isomorphic with cultural and psychological schemas — less rational, but pragmatic. Compared with residences in other regions, Huizhou residences and large Shanxi residences most have "Confucian air" and "merchant air"; Jiangnan water-town residences most have "literary air" and "spiritual air"; while Wenzhou residences lie between "Confucian air" and "wild air."

Residences with heavy "Confucian air" are rooted in square field systems, square city systems, and rational and ritual constraints, thus forming a square house system characterized by axial symmetry, depth development, strong introspective temperament, and courtyard type. Wenzhou residences are less rational and pragmatic, with creative purposes emphasizing practicality and creative methods adopting the "fit the form" principle with the background, forming an open "one" (linear) shape. From the perspective of village and residence site selection and layout, Wenzhou is mountainous, with scattered and fragmented fields in mountainous areas. To free up as much farmland as possible, people make their houses as close to the mountains as possible, following the mountains, waters, and terrain. Therefore, many houses and villages exhibit a temperament like flowing clouds and running water, as if growing out of the environment. This can be summarized by the eight characters "house and environment co-located, three principles (heavenly principle, geographical principle, physiological principle) unified."
