sections.name: 三、廊桥
sections.content_zh:
三、廊桥

桥和亭廊结合也是温州乡公共建筑中的一个特色。这种形式的桥，地方志记载不少，现在在平阳县、泰顺县还能看到，尤其是泰顺县还存八九座，《中国桥梁史》、《中国名胜辞典》两书已有收录。该县泗溪镇下桥村的"泗溪上、下桥"（照12-24，照12-25）、"薛家桥（照12-26）、刘家桥、永庆桥、祭下桥"等便是其中之典型。泗溪上桥为清乾隆十年（公元1746年）建造，木撑架式、单跨、八字形。上桥总长39.6m、宽5.9m、净跨27m，桥台用花岗岩石块垒筑于两岸山崖之上，桥底由七节主拱骨纵向并列，并与横向拱骨用榫铆连成一体，桥面铺木板，上建长廊式桥屋15间，中间三间抬高屋面，形成一楼阁式、单檐、歇山顶，屋上盖青瓦，两侧衬挡风板。为加宽通道，中间梁架用五架抬梁式。桥屋两端为歇山式屋面，左右两翼角高翘，从横断面看过去，分不清是桥是亭。泗溪下桥长51.7m、宽6.1m，有20间桥屋，其构件、造型与上桥相似。这两座桥相传是师徒先后分头建造的，故俗称"姐妹桥"。

泰顺众多的廊桥，按其承重的结构可分为石拱桥、石梁桥、木拱桥、木石混合结构桥。其中的木拱桥，结构尤为特殊，当地人称为"蜈蚣桥"，我国古建筑专家、同济大学路秉杰教授称之为"蜈蚣结构"，大加赞赏这个名称好，生动、形象又准确科学，反映了该结构的基本特征。比"虹桥"一词好得多，在现存的"蜈蚣桥"中，泗溪的姐妹双桥当属其中的翘楚。

路秉杰先生将这类桥的基本结构形式追溯到北宋名画《清明上河图》（张择端所作）中的"虹桥"。其结构的基本组合单元是六根杆件，纵向四根，横向两根，平面上呈井字结构，路先生并用筷子搭出一个拱桥的模型到处讲解这种桥梁结构的合理性，并撰文称之为"中国一绝"。由于桥是受压的，利用受压产生的摩擦力，构件之间就会越压越紧。这种结构，不用钉铆，用相同规格的杆件，穿插挤压，搭接而成。从力学上分析，上端的纵梁压在横梁上，横梁又压在相对一根纵梁上，相当于上下两根纵梁夹住一根横梁，因摩擦力的存在横梁不滑动，结构就不会破坏。此种结构，整体为拱形结构。因此，沿拱心线整体受压，不产生弯矩，就每一根杆件来说，又是最简单的简支梁，承受两种集中荷载。泗溪的姐妹双桥即采用经过演进的这种形式。这种虹桥结构，本来以为已经失传，后来在浙南、福建等地又陆续有所发现。在泰顺一地，竟有八座同类型的桥，如仙稔乡仙居桥等。

"蜈蚣结构"有很好的受压性能，只要两端部固定，桥就能很好地承受向下的荷载。但是，由于结构的特殊，桥受到向上的反弹力的水平的推力，故很容易失稳遭受破坏。为此，"蜈蚣桥"都采用了廊桥这种形式，桥上建廊非但不是负担，反而增加了稳定性，真是绝妙之极。同时，廊桥这一形式也使桥型更为优美，更可以成为人们休息、交流、交易的场所，从形式到内涵，都具有感人的艺术魅力与实用价值。泰顺洲岭毓文桥，桥廊上建有三层楼房，桥头建宗祠，是群众相会、活动的好场所（照12-27）。

平阳顺溪的永安桥（照12-28）、戈场桥（照12-29），直接架于涧谷间，形状和房屋一模一样，和山，水浑为一体，是民间创作的精品。
sections.content_en:
3. Covered Bridges (Langqiao)

The combination of bridges with pavilions and corridors is also a feature of Wenzhou's rural public buildings. This form of bridge is recorded in many local chronicles, and can still be seen today in Pingyang County and Taishun County, especially in Taishun County where eight or nine still survive. They have been included in the "History of Chinese Bridges" and "Dictionary of Chinese Scenic Spots." The "Sixi Upper and Lower Bridges" (photos 12-24, 12-25), "Xuejia Bridge" (photo 12-26), Liujia Bridge, Yongqing Bridge, and Jixia Bridge in Xiaqiao Village, Sixi Town, are typical examples. The Sixi Upper Bridge was built in the 10th year of Qing Qianlong (1746 AD), in timber-braced form, single-span, and八字 (eight-character) shape. The upper bridge has a total length of 39.6m, width of 5.9m, and clear span of 27m. The bridge abutments are built with granite blocks on the cliffs on both banks. The bridge bottom consists of seven main arch ribs arranged longitudinally in parallel, connected with transverse arch ribs by mortise and tenon joints into one body. The bridge deck is paved with wooden boards, with a long corridor-style bridge house of 15 bays built on top. The middle three bays have raised roofs, forming a pavilion-style, single-eave, hip-and-gable roof covered with blue tiles, with windbreak panels on both sides. To widen the passage, the middle beam frame uses five-frame post-and-lintel construction. Both ends of the bridge house have hip-and-gable roofs, with left and right wing corners upturned; from the cross-section, one cannot distinguish whether it is a bridge or a pavilion. The Sixi Lower Bridge is 51.7m long and 6.1m wide, with 20 bridge house bays; its components and form are similar to the upper bridge. These two bridges are said to have been built by a master and apprentice separately in succession, hence commonly called "Sister Bridges."

The numerous covered bridges in Taishun can be divided by load-bearing structure into stone arch bridges, stone beam bridges, timber arch bridges, and timber-stone composite structure bridges. Among them, the timber arch bridge has a particularly special structure, locally called "centipede bridge." Professor Lu Bingjie, an ancient Chinese architecture expert at Tongji University, calls it the "centipede structure," highly praising this name as vivid,形象, accurate, and scientific, reflecting the basic characteristics of this structure. It is much better than the term "rainbow bridge." Among the existing "centipede bridges," the Sister Double Bridges in Sixi are the outstanding ones.

Mr. Lu Bingjie traces the basic structural form of this type of bridge to the "rainbow bridge" in the famous Northern Song painting "Along the River During the Qingming Festival" (by Zhang Zeduan). Its basic structural unit is six members: four longitudinal and two transverse, forming a井 (well)-shaped structure in plane. Mr. Lu even used chopsticks to build a model of the arch bridge to explain the rationality of this bridge structure everywhere, and wrote articles calling it "a Chinese wonder." Because the bridge is under compression, using the friction force generated by compression, the members become tighter and tighter under pressure. This structure uses no nails or rivets, with members of the same specification interpenetrating,挤压, and搭接. From a mechanical analysis, the upper longitudinal beam presses on the transverse beam, which in turn presses on the opposite longitudinal beam, equivalent to the upper and lower longitudinal beams clamping one transverse beam; due to friction, the transverse beam does not slide, and the structure is not destroyed. This structure is整体 an arch structure. Therefore, along the arch center line it is整体 under compression, producing no bending moment; for each individual member, it is the simplest simply supported beam,承受 two concentrated loads. The Sister Double Bridges in Sixi adopt this evolved form. This rainbow bridge structure was originally thought to have been lost, but was later successively discovered in southern Zhejiang, Fujian, and other places. In Taishun alone, there are eight bridges of the same type, such as the Xianju Bridge in Xianren Township.

The "centipede structure" has excellent compression performance; as long as both ends are fixed, the bridge can well withstand downward loads. However, due to the special structure, the bridge receives horizontal thrust from upward rebound force, so it is easily destabilized and destroyed. For this reason, "centipede bridges" all adopt the covered bridge form; building a corridor on the bridge is not a burden but反而 increases stability — truly ingenious. At the same time, the covered bridge form also makes the bridge more beautiful, and can serve as a place for people to rest, communicate, and trade; from form to connotation, it has touching artistic charm and practical value. The Yuwen Bridge in Zhouling, Taishun, has a three-story building on the bridge corridor, with an ancestral hall at the bridgehead, a good place for the public to meet and活动 (photo 12-27).

The Yong'an Bridge (photo 12-28) and Gechang Bridge (photo 12-29) in Shunxi, Pingyang, are directly built across valleys, with shapes identical to houses, merging with mountains and waters into one body — masterpieces of folk creation.

sections.name: 四、牌坊
sections.content_zh:
四、牌坊

牌坊，俗称牌楼，其类型很多，本书收集的牌坊，主要是功德坊。一种是官位高且有政绩的，另一种是标志科举成就的。牌坊有嘉奖前人、效法后人、褒扬功德、光耀门庭、安定人心的作用。

牌坊由棂星门衍变而来。棂星即灵星，古代先民祭天先祭灵星，设计了一种门叫灵星门。类似作用的唐代有"华表"，宋元祭坛，通往祭坛长长神道前两旁设柱，到明朝又变成门的造型，并且日臻成熟完美，成为我国古建筑的一种重要形式。明代温州出了一批士人，其中不乏政绩卓著者，因此，御赐或乡人为之建造了很多牌坊，这些牌坊，也都带有温州乡土民居的某些特点。

1. 乐清南阁章纶牌坊群

邑人章纶（公元1413—1483年），明代进士，官授礼部主事，继升礼部侍郎。原有七座牌楼，现存五座，朝庭题额有"尚书""会魁""世进士"等五匾，均为木石结构，六柱，单间歇山顶，重檐式。清代大修过，仍保持明代建筑风格（照13-4，照13-5）。

2. 瓯海永强张璁祠牌坊

张璁（公元1475—1539年），永强人，明嘉靖朝内阁首辅，官至柱国少师兼太子太师、吏部尚书、华盖殿大学士。祠堂五间两进，两庑各七间，牌坊四柱，花岗岩砌筑，建于明代（照13-1）。

3. 永嘉花坦宪台牌楼

建于明弘治乙丑年（公元1505年），系温州知府李端、永嘉知县刘经纪念乡贤朱良濯（曾任四川按察司佥事）所建。四柱三楼式，木结构，高5.95m，宽6.28m，深5.05m（照13-3）。

4. 永嘉岩头进士牌楼

金昭（公元1576—1581），擢明嘉靖乙丑进士第，历官大理寺左、右寺副，升江西瑞州知府。

该牌楼四柱三楼式、木构，高7.63m，通面宽9.90m，通进深2.35m。明间两柱为方石柱，次间两柱为方木柱。柱脚前后置石抱鼓，柱础覆盆式。四角为木方柱，柱础是四角内削的方形石砌墩。明、次间均有前额、由额、额枋等，各施雀替、丁头拱。屋脊用薄砖砌成清水花脊，脊面刻如意花草，明间屋脊两端饰龙头吻，两垂脊脊端饰飞凤（照13-2）。
sections.content_en:
4. Memorial Archways (Paifang)

Paifang (memorial archways), commonly called pailou, have many types. The archways collected in this book are mainly merit archways. One type is for those with high official positions and political achievements; the other marks imperial examination achievements. Archways serve to reward predecessors, set examples for later generations, praise merit and virtue, glorify the family, and stabilize people's hearts.

Paifang evolved from the lingxing gate (lattice star gate). Lingxing means ling star; ancient ancestors first sacrificed to ling star when sacrificing to heaven, designing a gate called the ling star gate. Similar in function were the "huabiao" (ornamental columns) in the Tang dynasty; at Song-Yuan dynasty altars, columns were set on both sides before the long sacred path leading to the altar. By the Ming dynasty, this became a gate form, and gradually matured and perfected, becoming an important form of ancient Chinese architecture. In the Ming dynasty, Wenzhou produced a group of scholars, many with outstanding political achievements; therefore, many archways were built by imperial grant or by villagers, and these archways also carry certain characteristics of Wenzhou vernacular residences.

1. Zhang Lun Archway Group, Nange, Yueqing

Zhang Lun (1413-1483 AD), a native of the area, was a Ming dynasty jinshi (imperial examination graduate), appointed as a secretary in the Ministry of Rites, later promoted to Vice Minister of Rites. Originally there were seven archways, five still surviving. The imperial inscriptions include five plaques such as "Shangshu" (Minister), "Huikui" (Examination Champion), and "Shijinshi" (Generations of Jinshi). All are timber-stone structures, with six columns, single-bay hip-and-gable roof, double-eave style. Major renovations in the Qing dynasty still maintained the Ming dynasty architectural style (photos 13-4, 13-5).

2. Zhang Cong Shrine Archway, Yongqiang, Ouhai

Zhang Cong (1475-1539 AD), a native of Yongqiang, was the Grand Secretary of the Cabinet during the Ming Jiajing reign, reaching the position of Pillar of State, Junior Tutor, Crown Prince's Grand Tutor, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Huadian Hall. The shrine has five bays and two halls, with seven bays each on the two side wings. The archway has four columns, built of granite, constructed in the Ming dynasty (photo 13-1).

3. Xiantai Archway, Huatan, Yongjia

Built in the Ming Hongzhi Yichou year (1505 AD), it was constructed by Li Duan, Prefect of Wenzhou, and Liu Jing, County Magistrate of Yongjia, to commemorate local worthy Zhu Liangzhuo (who served as Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of Sichuan). Four-column three-story style, timber structure, 5.95m high, 6.28m wide, 5.05m deep (photo 13-3).

4. Jinshi Archway, Yantou, Yongjia

Jin Zhao (1576-1581), promoted to the Ming Jiajing Yichou jinshi degree, served as Left and Right Assistant of the Court of Judicial Review, and was promoted to Prefect of Ruizhou, Jiangxi.

This archway is four-column three-story style, timber structure, 7.63m high, 9.90m total width, 2.35m total depth. The two columns of the central bay are square stone columns, and the two columns of the side bays are square timber columns. Stone drum braces are placed before and after the column feet, with basin-shaped column bases. The four corners are timber square columns, with square stone piers with inward-cut corners as column bases. Both central and side bays have front architraves, secondary architraves, and header beams, each with sparrow braces and T-head brackets. The ridge is made of thin bricks into a plain decorative ridge, with auspicious flowers and plants carved on the ridge surface; both ends of the central bay ridge are decorated with dragon-head ornaments, and the ends of the two vertical ridges are decorated with flying phoenixes (photo 13-2).

key_terms.en: Zhang Lun archway group, Nange, Yueqing

chapters.name: 第五章 温州乡土建筑中的典型大屋

sections.name: 一、平阳顺溪陈氏古宅
sections.content_zh:
一、平阳顺溪陈氏古宅

平阳顺溪陈育球，明隆庆代人，其家庭繁衍传留下来七座大屋，可称浙南传统民居的典型，它对顺溪镇的风貌有结构性作用，民间有"青街竹，顺溪屋"之谚语（青街——附近镇名，盛产毛竹）。

七兄弟七座屋称老大份、老二份等。老大份最大，据内悬匾纪年及陈氏谱牒记载，该屋建于清乾（隆）、嘉（庆）年间，平面布局采用院落相套、纵深发展的形式，依三条纵横轴线，用回廊分隔成六个既独立又相联的庭院。总建筑面积4200m²，共有大小天井6个，套房99间，四周垒高墙。整幢建筑以中心轴线为主体，依次建有门台、门厅、中厅和后厅，两侧横厢有走马楼，厢后有廊厢别院。房舍分布错落有致。庭院毗连。回廊串接，过道相通。台门以方整块石垒底，长条白石砌成，悬山顶，铺青筒瓦，门台前左右分立旗杆石；前厅系木构平房，九开间，梁架为穿斗与抬梁混合式结构。明间抬梁，上设十一架梁，立柱与檐柱间设单步梁与双步梁，边缝梁架分心造，前后用搭牵，并在三架梁上设驼峰与瓜柱，檐柱柱头置一斗三升；柱础为方形青石；屋面为悬山顶，铺平瓦，正脊两端饰有飞吻；门窗雕镂精致，图案形象生动；地面铺正方形青砖，排列有序；整幢建筑布局恢宏，构建工巧，古朴典雅。

照14-1，照14-2所示，户侯弟为老四份，主政第为老七份。

老四份1845m²，37间，有户侯第等四个匾，内有花厅、花园、鱼池。老七份2730m²，58间，内有10条路巷、门台三间，两旁三对旗杆，厅内有"司马第""文元""萱荫恒春""名端金玉"等五个匾额（图8-1，图8-2）。
sections.content_en:
1. Chen Family Ancient Residence, Shunxi, Pingyang

Chen Yuqiu of Shunxi, Pingyang, was a person of the Ming Longqing period. His family multiplied and passed down seven large houses, which can be called typical of traditional residences in southern Zhejiang. They play a structural role in the appearance of Shunxi Town, with a folk saying: "Qingjie bamboo, Shunxi houses" (Qingjie — a nearby town name, rich in bamboo).

The seven brothers' seven houses are called the eldest branch, second branch, etc. The eldest branch is the largest. According to the hanging plaque date and Chen family genealogy records, this house was built during the Qing Qianlong and Jiaqing periods. Its plane layout adopts the form of nested courtyards and depth development, following three vertical and horizontal axes, divided by corridors into six independent yet connected courtyards. The total building area is 4200m², with 6 sky wells of various sizes, 99 suites, and high walls surrounding all sides. The entire building takes the central axis as the main body,依次 building the gate platform, gate hall, central hall, and rear hall. The side wings have "galloping horse towers" (zouma lou), with corridor-wing side yards behind the wings. The rooms are arranged in a错落有致 manner. Courtyards are adjacent. Corridors connect, passages communicate. The gate platform is built with square whole stones at the base and long white stones, with an overhanging gable roof covered with blue筒 tiles; flagpole stones stand separately on the left and right in front of the gate hall. The front hall is a timber single-story building, nine bays, with a beam frame of mixed column-and-tie and post-and-lintel structure. The central bay uses post-and-lintel, with an eleven-frame beam on top; between the columns and eave columns are single-step and double-step beams; the side bay beam frames use split-center construction, with tie beams front and rear, and camel humps and short columns on the three-frame beams; the eave column heads have one-dou-three-sheng brackets; column bases are square bluestone; the roof is overhanging gable, covered with flat tiles, with flying ornaments at both ends of the main ridge; doors and windows are exquisitely carved with vivid patterns; the ground is paved with square blue bricks in orderly arrangement; the entire building has a magnificent layout, ingenious construction, and is simple and elegant.

As shown in photos 14-1 and 14-2, the Houhou Di (Marquis Household) is the fourth branch, and the Zhuzheng Di (Governor's Residence) is the seventh branch.

The fourth branch is 1845m², 37 rooms, with four plaques including Houhou Di, containing a flower hall, garden, and fish pond. The seventh branch is 2730m², 58 rooms, with 10 alleys inside, a three-bay gate platform, three pairs of flagpoles on both sides, and five plaques in the hall including "Sima Di" (Sima Residence), "Wenyuan" (Literary Origin), "Xuanyin Hengchun" (Eternal Spring Shade), and "Mingduan Jinyu" (Precious Name) (Figures 8-1, 8-2).

key_terms.en: Chen family ancient residence, Shunxi, Pingyang
Zouma lou (galloping horse tower, corridor wing)

sections.name: 二、永嘉芙蓉村陈氏司马大屋
sections.content_zh:
二、永嘉芙蓉村陈氏司马大屋

位于永嘉楠溪江风景区的芙蓉村。村西北有陈姓家族聚居的邸宅，俗称陈氏大屋，始建于清朝康熙年间，落地36间，占地1公顷。平面为二进庭院组成，横向布局形式，沿中轴线布置照壁、大门、庭院、厅堂。厅堂分主次，主庭居前，每个厅堂辟一小庭分隔。大屋结构采用传统的六架三柱（或四柱）带檐廊的抬梁式木构架；屋面采用悬山屋顶，清水砖墙，青砖规整，灰缝细少，衬以青砖的自然花纹。所有木作用料考究，以梓木为柱，显得凝重坚实，且很少使用油漆，以表露木质和纹理的自然美。大屋前庭花园一隅，至今犹留四楹学塾遗址；青石门楣和柱础上的石雕，及梁枋、雀替、椽头、门窗格扇上的木雕，都有千刻万镂传神之作（图7-1，图7-2）。
sections.content_en:
2. Chen Family Sima Large Residence, Furong Village, Yongjia

Located in Furong Village in the Nanxi River Scenic Area of Yongjia. In the northwest of the village there is a residence where the Chen family clan lives, commonly called the Chen Family Large Residence. It was first built during the Qing Kangxi period, with 36 rooms on the ground and covering 1 hectare. The plane consists of two courtyards, in a horizontal layout form, with a screen wall, main gate, courtyard, and hall arranged along the central axis. Halls are divided into primary and secondary, with the main courtyard in front, and each hall has a small courtyard for separation. The large residence structure adopts the traditional six-frame three-column (or four-column) post-and-lintel timber frame with eaves corridors; the roof uses overhanging gable roofs, with plain brick walls, regular blue bricks, fine and few mortar joints, set off by the natural patterns of blue bricks. All woodwork uses carefully selected materials, with catalpa wood (zimu) as columns, appearing dignified and solid, and rarely uses paint, to reveal the natural beauty of wood texture and grain. In a corner of the front garden of the large residence, the ruins of a four-bay school still remain today; the stone carvings on the bluestone door lintels and column bases, and the wood carvings on beams, sparrow braces, rafter heads, and door/window lattice panels, are all masterpieces of exquisite carving (Figures 7-1, 7-2).

key_terms.term: 永嘉芙蓉村陈氏司马大屋
key_terms.en: Chen family Sima large residence, Furong Village, Yongjia

sections.name: 三、泰顺雪溪石门楼
sections.content_zh:
三、泰顺雪溪石门楼

石门楼为泰顺县雪溪乡桥西村胡氏住宅，迄今已有八代，第四代胡维基是现代著名数学家。

石门楼背靠山，面向田野，雪溪在屋前流过，隔溪远眺是高耸的笔架山。整栋建筑处于符合中国风水追求的"背山、面水、前有朝山、案山"的理想环境中。从正屋二层远眺，令人心旷神怡，因此在门楼面对正屋一侧，有"山辉川媚"一匾，反之，站在下堂走道看主屋，青山为靠，故门楼另一侧又书："日拥祥云"四字。

平面布局轴对称，而大门则依风水学原理偏于一边。石门楼有二进，分上下两堂，下堂左右两侧各有厢房，下堂院内被中央两道花墙一分为三。上堂前有一个大内院，正屋面阔七间，进深五架。上下堂高差1.2m。石门楼的屋顶为双层檐，两端各有一个纵向的双坡顶，伸入大坡顶之下，可以说是歇山顶的一种发展，这种形式是温州民居的一种特色。下堂山墙弓背、清水墙，和众多的飞檐翘角相辉映，造成了玲珑辉煌的气势（照14-3）。
sections.content_en:
3. Shimenlou (Stone Gate Tower), Xuexi, Taishun

Shimenlou is the Hu family residence in Qiaoxi Village, Xuexi Township, Taishun County. It has been eight generations so far, and the fourth generation Hu Weiji is a famous modern mathematician.

Shimenlou backs against mountains, faces fields, with Xuexi Stream flowing in front of the house, and across the stream in the distance is the towering Bijia Mountain (Brush Holder Mountain). The entire building is in an ideal environment符合 Chinese feng shui pursuit of "backing mountains, facing water, with facing mountains and desk mountains in front." Looking into the distance from the second floor of the main house is refreshing and delightful; therefore, on the side of the gate tower facing the main house, there is a plaque "Shanhui Chuanmei" (Mountains Shining, Rivers Charming). Conversely, standing in the lower hall corridor looking at the main house, with green mountains as backing, the other side of the gate tower is inscribed with four characters "Riyong Xiangyun" (Daily Embracing Auspicious Clouds).

The plane layout is axisymmetric, while the main gate is偏 to one side according to feng shui principles. Shimenlou has two halls, divided into upper and lower halls. The lower hall has wing rooms on both left and right sides, and the lower hall courtyard is divided into three by two central flower walls. In front of the upper hall is a large inner courtyard; the main house is seven bays wide and five frames deep. The height difference between upper and lower halls is 1.2m. The roof of Shimenlou is double-eaved, with a longitudinal double-slope roof at each end extending under the large slope roof, which can be said to be a development of the hip-and-gable roof; this form is a characteristic of Wenzhou residences. The lower hall's gable walls are bow-backed and plain brick walls, reflecting with numerous flying eaves and upturned corners, creating an exquisite and magnificent momentum (photo 14-3).

key_terms.en: Backing mountains, facing water, facing/desk mountains (feng shui)

sections.name: 四、泰顺三魁下武洋林家厝
sections.content_zh:
四、泰顺三魁下武洋林家厝

房屋始建于清乾隆年间，第一代屋主林谷芳。房屋选址运用了中国传统的风水理论，房屋靠山，山上树木郁葱，屋前是大片稻田，主轴线正对之案山，山形起伏有致，左右两为山口。在案山与稻田之间，一条蜿蜒的溪水潺潺流过，溪畔古木参天。林家厝实际上就是一组容住居、休憩、耕读为一体的综合建筑群。

建筑群由上下两部分组成，用窄巷联系家庭生产、生活活动。日常对外交往主要在此巷进出，重要客人或礼仪活动才从正门出入。二进九院八个门台，居室的空间构成反映出当时居住形式的环农业特征和屋主的宇宙观（图9-1，图9-2，照14-4）。
sections.content_en:
4. Lin Family Residence, Xiawuyang, Sankui, Taishun

The house was first built during the Qing Qianlong period, with the first-generation owner Lin Gufang. The house site selection applied traditional Chinese feng shui theory: the house backs against mountains with lush trees on the mountain, in front of the house is a large paddy field, the main axis faces the desk mountain (anshan) with undulating mountain form, and the left and right are mountain passes. Between the desk mountain and the paddy field, a winding stream flows gurgling, with ancient trees towering by the stream. The Lin family residence is actually a comprehensive building group integrating residence, rest, and farming-studying.

The building group consists of upper and lower parts, connected by narrow alleys for family production and daily activities. Daily external communication mainly enters and exits through this alley; important guests or ceremonial activities enter and exit through the main gate. With two halls, nine courtyards, and eight gate platforms, the spatial composition of the rooms reflects the agricultural-surrounding characteristics of the residential form at that time and the owner's worldview (Figures 9-1, 9-2, photo 14-4).

key_terms.term: 泰顺三魁下武洋林家厝
key_terms.en: Lin family residence, Xiawuyang, Sankui, Taishun

sections.name: 五、泰顺三魁镇庵前村张氏七榴九榴
sections.content_zh:
五、泰顺三魁镇庵前村张氏七榴、九榴

"榴"是指房屋开间，七榴即七开间。七榴、九榴为张氏两兄弟所建，九榴由张守京建于清道光年间，光绪年间失火，守京公长子冠英重建。七榴后建，实兄弟两同住，两厢各就其主。大堂共享，一楼大堂为婚宴用，二楼大堂祭祖，这样可以相互牵制，以维系祖辈家业，两兄弟皆为乡贤。九榴屋主张守京，千总衔，号鼎候。重建之九榴（今存屋）屋主冠英、贡生（图10-1，图10-2，照14-5）。
sections.content_en:
5. Zhang Family Qiliu and Jiuliu, Anqian Village, Sankui Town, Taishun

"Liu" refers to house bays; qiliu means seven bays. Qiliu and Jiuliu were built by two Zhang brothers. Jiuliu was built by Zhang Shoujing during the Qing Daoguang period; it caught fire during the Guangxu period and was rebuilt by Shoujing's eldest son Guanying. Qiliu was built later; actually the two brothers lived together, with each wing belonging to its owner. The main hall is shared: the first-floor main hall is for wedding banquets, and the second-floor main hall is for ancestor worship, so they can restrain each other to maintain the ancestral family business. Both brothers were village worthies. The Jiuliu owner Zhang Shoujing held the rank of qianzong (military officer), with the hao (courtesy name) Dinghou. The rebuilt Jiuliu (existing house) owner is Guanying, a gongsheng (tribute student) (Figures 10-1, 10-2, photo 14-5).

sections.name: 六、永嘉埭头松风水月宅
sections.content_zh:
六、永嘉埭头松风水月宅

永嘉埭头村在清代是一个建筑专业村，这些有技艺的人，可称为淮文人学士。他们外出创业，挣了钱以后回家乡施展自己的技艺和经济实力，整个村子古宅、门楼、宗祠、花墙争艳斗丽。松风水月宅是其中一个典型，该宅的理水和入口极具特色。宅院外地形下降1.5m，挖一方塘，设有两道门，第一道门是形式简单的砖门楼，第二道门分为互为垂直的两片，一片与住宅垂直，供人出入，另一片与住宅平行，前临水池，门洞里装上美人靠，人可凭栏望见池边浣衣的妇女笑语对话，住宅内外空间与生活情景水乳交融（照14-6）。
sections.content_en:
6. Songfeng Shuiyue Residence, Daitou, Yongjia

Daitou Village in Yongjia was an architectural professional village in the Qing dynasty. These skilled people can be called Huai literati and scholars. They went out to start businesses, and after earning money, returned to their hometown to施展 their skills and economic strength; the entire village's ancient houses, gate towers, ancestral halls, and flower walls compete in beauty. The Songfeng Shuiyue (Pine Wind Water Moon) Residence is a typical example among them, with its water management and entrance being highly distinctive. The terrain outside the residence drops 1.5m, with a square pond dug out. There are two gates: the first gate is a simple brick gate tower, and the second gate is divided into two mutually perpendicular sections — one perpendicular to the residence for people to enter and exit, and the other parallel to the residence, facing the pool in front, with a "beauty's lean" (meirenkao) installed in the gate opening; people can lean on the railing to see laundry women by the pool chatting and laughing, with the interior and exterior spaces of the residence and life scenes blending seamlessly (photo 14-6).

chapters.name: 第六章 温州乡土建筑文化寻踪

sections.name: 一、闷热湿的气候条件培育出居屋制作的仿生原则
sections.content_zh:
一、闷、热、湿的气候条件培育出居屋制作的仿生原则

温州的自然条件有三个特色：一是位于光、热、雨资源的高值区（平均日照时数1700～2400h，年平均气温16～18℃，日平均气温大于10℃的年平均积温在4500～5600℃之间，年平均降雨量1800mm左右）；二有光温互补、雨热同步的特点，即天气冷（冬季）时日照百分率高，热的时候（夏季）雨水多，5—6月梅雨连绵，7—9月台风雨频繁；三是湿度高，秋季温度不很高，但因湿度高而显得闷热。

光和雨是古人建房时要对付的两个主要问题，太热要防止太阳直射屋内，要挡雨，要防止台风雨飘进屋内，由于台风大又要求抗风。或许是受了亚热带阔叶树的启发，古人首先不是从建筑材料或墙体构造上解决这两大问题，而是让房子像树一样长很多叶——于是产生了各种各样的檐；一层平面解决不了防潮防湿，房子就向上长，又产生了重檐、腰檐等，成为温州民居的一大特色。这可叫做古人建筑创作的仿生原则。

开敞通透，也是顺应光和雨的结果。上面讲过，温州气候除了温度高和多雨的特点外，闷和湿也是它的特点，于是提出房子的通风、防潮、防湿问题。当然，檐也有通和防的功能，但光靠遮和挡两个办法还不能从根本上解决这个问题，于是想到了透和漏两个办法，形成开敞通透的特色。
sections.content_en:
1. Stuffy, Hot, Humid Climate Conditions Cultivate the Bionic Principle of House Making

Wenzhou's natural conditions have three characteristics: first, it is located in a high-value area of light, heat, and rainfall resources (average sunshine hours 1700-2400h, annual average temperature 16-18°C, annual average accumulated temperature above 10°C between 4500-5600°C, annual average rainfall about 1800mm); second, it has the characteristics of light-temperature complementarity and rain-heat synchronization, i.e., when the weather is cold (winter) the sunshine percentage is high, when it is hot (summer) there is much rain, with continuous plum rain from May to June, and frequent typhoon rains from July to September; third, high humidity, with autumn temperatures not very high but appearing stuffy due to high humidity.

Light and rain were the two main problems ancient people had to deal with when building houses. Too hot means preventing direct sunlight from entering the house, blocking rain, preventing typhoon rain from blowing into the house, and due to strong typhoons, requiring wind resistance. Perhaps inspired by subtropical broadleaf trees, ancient people first solved these two major problems not from building materials or wall construction, but by making the house grow many leaves like a tree — thus various types of eaves were created; one-story planes could not solve moisture prevention, so houses grew upward, creating double eaves, waist eaves, etc., becoming a major feature of Wenzhou residences. This can be called the bionic principle of ancient architectural creation.

Openness and transparency are also the result of adapting to light and rain. As mentioned above, besides high temperature and rainy characteristics, Wenzhou's climate is also stuffy and humid, thus raising the issues of ventilation, moisture prevention, and damp prevention for houses. Of course, eaves also have functions of ventilation and prevention, but relying only on shading and blocking cannot fundamentally solve this problem; thus the two methods of transparency and leakage were conceived, forming the characteristic of openness and transparency.

sections.name: 二、农业范式辐射出居屋的环农业特征
sections.content_zh:
二、农业范式辐射出居屋的环农业特征

我国位于温带、亚热带生物富集区，古代以农立国，以种植经济为基本的生产方式。人们日出而作，日入而息，整天和泥土打交道，农闲时祭山祭水祭祖先，穷者力田致富，富了就想买田买屋，选择职业以耕读为上，士大夫一旦得志，其精神日趋求田问舍，做官的以"劝农"为本，退休的要荣归故里，很多美的事物都带田字，如称神农为"田祖"，叫老农为"田父"，指故乡为"田里"，有田方为福，福从田地起，并喻一切滋生之物为田，如砚田、心田，一句话，个人及社会的一切活动和思维都是以农业为中心，环绕着土地展开的。人们在这种生活方式中展开了和自然的关系，找到自己在宇宙中的位置，产生了深刻的山水和土地观念，并使自己的思想方法、审美情趣、价值观念，都打上了土地的烙印。这些，可叫做古代中国生活方式的环农业特征。这一特征，很大程度上导致了传统建筑的恋土品格以及由此引起的内聚心理。在形式上，表现出来的最大特征是出现了民居的门—院—屋三段式模式。

古代中国家庭之家的完整概念应包含三层意思：①《诗·周南》谓宜其家室，即一门之内谓之家，这是家的"物"的概念。② 有夫有妇然后为家，这是家的"人"的概念。③ 受田百亩为夫家，这是大典用"社会"概念。房屋仅仅是家的居住部分，称作家室，住房之外，还必须有个院子，故古代又把家叫作家园。这个院落，是家屋和农业联系的纽带，是田地的伸延，是农耕活动的继续，有纳天地于家的精神功能，也是家庭地位、文化素质的重要表征。曾国藩把养鱼、喂猪、种竹、种菜列为家政四要，他说，这样做一方面可以让人在墙外就看到家庭的生气，走进院子后，又看见一片繁荣景象。可见，农耕时代的家庭院落是多么重要，由于有了这个空间，住房本身反而退到次要地位了。

农业经济对温州乡土民居的影响，还表现在平面布局、立面造型诸方面。比如H形住宅的形成过程，就是家庭发展的过程。原先一字形住宅，正间即堂屋为放祖先灵位、会客、设祭行礼、婚丧大典用，堂屋的两边为卧室，尽端才是厨房，子女多的家庭，一字形房屋不够用，就添两厢，变成门形。正房、厢房、门台合成的院落比较整洁，有些辅助房如厕所、猪栏不宜在屋前，于是向后发展，变成H形住宅。这种住宅实际上有前后两个院落（或天井）。H形住宅也可能是一次造成的，这样的家庭，一两代之后，就要析产分灶，于是再向纵深或左右发展，又成了日形，田形或更多的院落（天井）。

农业经济时代家务多，坐在门窗多而空透的室内还嫌太热，于是产生了半露天的檐廊。该空间成为家庭日常生活的主要场所，剥豆、掰玉米、手工业、纺织、聊天、读书、游戏、夏天进餐都在廊下。《隋书·地理志》、《齐民要术》等书记载：古代温州蚕桑业非常发达，一年有八次蚕丝生产，家庭纺织也很兴旺、妇女往往能"夜浣纱而旦成布"。这就是温州经济史上闻名全国的"八辈蚕"和"鸡鸣布"。这两项家庭生产活动，季节性很强，都要求有可通可隔、灵活变化的空间和良好的避晒、通风条件。这也是温州檐廊或重檐生成的机制。

农家做饭的柴草很多，不能都放在屋里，以及很多杂物需堆放在屋边，因此，需要深檐遮挡。有些食物、种子、菜干等，需晾晒于家畜不能到的高处，于是产生了腰檐、重檐、檐箱等。

把时间向前推，古瓯越人的主要经济活动是渔猎。《山海经·海内南经》曰："瓯居海中"。《逸周书·王会解》称"东越海蛤，瓯人蝉蛇"。可以设想最初的瓯人是以舟楫为家或以水阑式结构形式为居室的。到了农耕社会，人们向山林谷处移动，以棚为室居。因此，"船"、"棚"可认为是各种各样檐的原型。
sections.content_en:
2. Agricultural Paradigm Radiates the Agricultural-Surrounding Characteristic of Residences

China is located in a temperate and subtropical biodiversity-rich region. In ancient times, the nation was founded on agriculture, with planting economy as the basic production mode. People worked at sunrise and rested at sunset, dealing with soil all day. In slack farming seasons, they sacrificed to mountains, waters, and ancestors. The poor worked hard in fields to become rich, and when rich they wanted to buy land and houses; career choices prioritized farming and studying; once scholar-officials achieved success, their spirit increasingly sought land and houses; officials took "encouraging agriculture" as fundamental; retirees wanted to return to their hometowns in glory. Many beautiful things carry the character "tian" (field): for example, calling Shennong "Tianzu" (Field Ancestor), old farmers "Tianfu" (Field Father), hometown "Tianli" (In the Fields), having fields means fortune, fortune arises from fields, and metaphorically all growing things are fields, such as "yantian" (inkstone field) and "xintian" (heart field). In a word, all activities and thinking of individuals and society are centered on agriculture, unfolding around the land. In this lifestyle, people developed their relationship with nature, found their position in the universe,产生了 profound mountain-water and land concepts, and imprinted their thinking methods, aesthetic tastes, and values with the mark of land. These can be called the agricultural-surrounding characteristic of ancient Chinese lifestyle. This characteristic largely led to the earth-loving character of traditional architecture and the resulting inward-gathering psychology. In form, the most prominent characteristic is the emergence of the gate-courtyard-house three-stage model of residences.

The complete concept of family in ancient China should include three layers of meaning: ① "Book of Songs · Zhou Nan" says "appropriate for her family and house," i.e., within one gate is called home, this is the "object" concept of home. ② Having a husband and wife then makes a home, this is the "person" concept of home. ③ Receiving one hundred mu of fields makes a husband's family, this is the grand code's "social" concept. The house is only the residential part of the home, called "jiashi" (family room); besides the house, there must also be a courtyard, hence ancient times also called home "jiayuan" (family garden). This courtyard is the link between the house and agriculture, an extension of fields, a continuation of farming activities, with the spiritual function of bringing heaven and earth into the home, and also an important表征 of family status and cultural quality. Zeng Guofan listed raising fish, feeding pigs, planting bamboo, and growing vegetables as the four essentials of household management. He said that doing so allows people to see the vitality of the family outside the wall, and after entering the courtyard, see a prosperous scene. It can be seen how important the family courtyard was in the agricultural era; because of this space, the house itself反而 receded to a secondary position.

The influence of agricultural economy on Wenzhou vernacular residences is also manifested in plane layout and facade modeling. For example, the formation process of H-shaped residences is the process of family development. Originally one-line residences: the central bay, i.e., the main hall, was for placing ancestral spirit tablets, receiving guests, holding sacrifices and ceremonies, weddings and funerals; both sides of the main hall were bedrooms, with the kitchen at the far end. For families with many children, one-line houses were insufficient, so two wings were added, becoming "门" (U) shape. The courtyard formed by the main house, wings, and gate platform is relatively tidy; some auxiliary rooms such as toilets and pigsties are not suitable in front of the house, so they develop backward, becoming H-shaped residences. This type of residence actually has front and rear courtyards (or sky wells). H-shaped residences may also be built at once; such families, after one or two generations, need to divide property and kitchens, thus developing further in depth or left/right, becoming "日" (sun) shape, "田" (field) shape, or more courtyards (sky wells).

In the agricultural economy era, there was much housework; sitting in rooms with many and transparent windows and doors was still too hot, thus semi-open eaves corridors were created. This space became the main place for family daily life: shelling beans, breaking corn, handicrafts, weaving, chatting, reading, games, and summer meals all happened under the corridors. "Sui Shu · Geography Annals" and "Qimin Yaoshu" record: ancient Wenzhou's sericulture was very developed, with eight silk productions per year, and family weaving was also prosperous; women often "washed yarn at night and finished cloth at dawn." This is the nationally famous "eight-generation silkworm" and "rooster-crow cloth" in Wenzhou's economic history. These two family production activities are highly seasonal, both requiring spaces that can be open or closed, flexible and changeable, with good sun-shading and ventilation conditions. This is also the mechanism for the generation of Wenzhou's eaves corridors or double eaves.

Farmers had much firewood and grass for cooking, which could not all be placed inside, and many杂物 needed to be stacked beside the house, therefore requiring deep eaves for shelter. Some food, seeds, dried vegetables, etc., needed to be dried in high places inaccessible to livestock, thus creating waist eaves, double eaves, eave boxes, etc.

Pushing time forward, the main economic activity of the ancient Ouyue people was fishing and hunting. "Classic of Mountains and Seas · South of the Inner Seas" says: "Ou resides in the sea." "Yi Zhou Shu · Wang Hui Jie" states: "Dongyue sea clams, Ou people cicada snakes." It can be imagined that the earliest Ou people made boats their homes or used stilt-style structures as residences. By the agricultural society, people moved to mountain forests and valleys, living in sheds. Therefore, "boat" and "shed" can be considered the prototypes of various eaves.

key_terms.en: Boat and shed as eave prototypes

sections.name: 三、天人合一的时空观孕化为生动玲珑的屋顶
sections.content_zh:
三、"天人合一"的时空观孕化为生动、玲珑的屋顶

中国传统建筑对第五立面（屋面）的重视程度远远超过其他立面。这是古代居住图式和"天人合一"的哲学思想孕化出来的结果。古人对"天"的认识有六种意义，其中一义为天是有意志、有灵感的，它支配人间的一切。这一思想派生出古代集祭、卜、祀、社、屋为一体的居住图式。祭为祭天，卜为巫术预测，祀是纪念祖先，社为国家，屋指家。祭、卜、祀的基本指向都在头上，因此，把屋顶做得非常生动壮丽，用它满足心理上壮威的需要，以及祈祷天的保佑。"天人合一"的基本思想是：古人以"天、地、人"为宇宙之三才，视天、地、人为一体，以天人关系的主轴展开自己的思维，并且构筑出一个"以象制器"的创作方法体系。何谓"以象制器"，《易·系辞上》曰："圣人有以见天下之赜，而拟诸其形容，象其物宜，是故谓之象"，"天垂象，见吉凶，圣人象之"，即古人是用象征符号概括模拟自然之象而成人工之"象"（这个象就是器）。屋面形式上把人和天隔开，这对于古人来说是诚惶诚恐的，因此，一定要从屋顶上寻找和天通融的东西，古代把房屋叫做"屋宇"，就是这种心理的反映。光有这么一个名字还不行，还必须把头顶的建筑物构件搞得和天象接近一些，才能满足心理平衡。清代陈梦雷《周易浅述》曰："栋，屋脊，承而上者；宇，椽也，垂而下者，故曰上栋下宇。风雨动于上，栋宇复于下，固天之象，又取壮固之意。"《周易·说卦传》曰："乾为天，震为雷，为龙，震乾上，壮固的卦象为雷鸣龙腾，气势威武壮美"。可见，古人把屋面当作主要立面，把坡屋面发展成反曲面，屋角做成翘角，屋脊做成反弓形，并且把各种狩猎的兽身装饰在屋顶，是对天象的反响及呼应，是把居住主体（人）的生命融进宇宙流程的一种寄托。古代的木匠在盖房前一般都要静心修性，具有契合"天意"的意义，是天人感应的表现。
sections.content_en:
3. "Unity of Heaven and Humanity" Time-Space View Gestates into Vivid and Exquisite Roofs

Traditional Chinese architecture attaches far more importance to the fifth facade (roof surface) than to other facades. This is the result gestated from ancient residential patterns and the philosophical thought of "unity of heaven and humanity" (tian ren he yi). Ancient people had six meanings for their understanding of "heaven," one of which was that heaven has will and inspiration, dominating everything in the human world. This thought派生 the ancient residential pattern integrating sacrifice, divination, commemoration, state, and house. Sacrifice means sacrificing to heaven; divination means shamanic prediction; commemoration means remembering ancestors; state means the country; house means home. The basic direction of sacrifice, divination, and commemoration is all upward, therefore, roofs were made very vivid and magnificent, to satisfy the psychological need for imposing power and to pray for heaven's blessing. The basic thought of "unity of heaven and humanity" is: ancient people took "heaven, earth, and humanity" as the three talents of the universe, regarding heaven, earth, and humanity as one body,展开 their thinking around the main axis of heaven-humanity relationship, and constructing a creative method system of "using images to make vessels." What does "using images to make vessels" mean? "I Ching · Xici Shang" says: "The sages, seeing the subtleties of the world, simulated their forms and images, representing their appropriate qualities, hence called them images"; "Heaven displays images, showing fortune and misfortune, and the sages imitate them" — that is, ancient people used symbolic signs to summarize and simulate natural images into artificial "images" (this image is the vessel). The roof form separates humanity from heaven, which made ancient people feel apprehensive; therefore, they must find something on the roof that communicates with heaven. Ancient people called houses "wuyu" (house-eaves), which is a reflection of this psychology. Just having such a name was not enough; they must also make the building components overhead closer to celestial phenomena to satisfy psychological balance. Chen Menglei of the Qing dynasty wrote in "Zhouyi Qianshu" (Brief Exposition of the I Ching): "Dong (ridge beam) is the roof ridge, bearing upward; Yu (eaves) is the rafter, hanging downward, hence called upper dong lower yu. Wind and rain move above, dong and yu cover below,固 the image of heaven, also taking the meaning of strength and solidity." "I Ching · Shuoguo Zhuan" says: "Qian is heaven, Zhen is thunder, is dragon; Zhen above Qian, the strong and solid hexagram image is thunder roaring and dragon leaping, with a powerful and majestic momentum." It can be seen that ancient people regarded the roof as the main facade, developed sloped roofs into reverse curved surfaces, made roof corners into upturned corners, made ridges into reverse bow shapes, and decorated roofs with various hunting beast bodies — this is a response and echo to celestial phenomena, a sustenance of integrating the life of the residential subject (humanity) into the cosmic process. Ancient carpenters generally had to calm their minds and cultivate their nature before building houses, which has the meaning of契合 "heaven's will," a manifestation of heaven-humanity感应.

key_terms.en: Tian ren he yi (unity of heaven and humanity)

sections.name: 四、民俗与温州乡土建筑文化
sections.content_zh:
四、民俗与温州乡土建筑文化

"风俗"是影响民居类型和风格的重要因素。"风"指国风，它影响、形成民居的共性；"俗"指民俗，造就民居的个性。

分析第一章所述，温州民俗有如下特点：① 活动频繁，从正月到腊月，遇初一或十五，逢三、八、二、七日子等皆有民俗活动。② 活动面广，从城市、集镇到农村，无论年长岁小，全民参与。③ 聚集性强，很多活动不是家庭式的，而是社团性、地方性的，大家都集中在一个场所或赶到一个地方去。④ 竞争性强，很多民俗活动带有竞赛性，如划龙舟。有的形式上不是竞赛，而实质上具有竞赛成份，如舞龙灯、灯节、"花祭"等，参与者以村或街道或家庭为单位，都有比一比谁搞得好的意识。⑤从文化层面讲，带有浓厚的巫文化成份，既敬神又娱己。

民俗活动需要载体或场所，其载体多为建筑，场所多为公共用地。如庙台戏，其戏台是临时搭建的，一般选择在村子的公共空地上或晒谷场或宗祠前的平地上，也或在山脚或几条路口交汇处、水边、桥头。拦街福活动中的花祭（摆盆景、陈花卉）多摆在门前、檐廊下，也有集中在某一公共建筑内的。至于神祀，多数需建有神庙、祠堂。

民俗活动的结果，从精神上提升了人们的创造力和竞争性，从而刺激了建筑营造活动，成了乡土建筑的动力，并且影响了建筑及装修的风格。如温瑞塘河是唐宋代为开发圩田而开挖的一条内河，明清代由于祭神活动需要，人们利用船揖之便在两岸搭戏台演戏，修建了十多个庙，时称"水台"，祭神活动时，请地方戏剧班演戏，同时商贩云集形成独具特色的"会市"，并逐渐形成一个个村镇，加上交通、农田开发等原因，形成今天摆在世人面前的集镇首尾相接的风貌。

温州的神祭有祭土地神，有祀古代职司如"文昌庙"、"药王庙"等，有祭历史名人的如神农、徐偃王、王羲之等，也有祭感应神祇的如"忠精圣王"、"胡公大帝"等，形成了温州乡土建筑宗庙祠堂遍布的景观特色。温州民俗活动中的正月元宵灯会舞龙，三月三拦街福，端午扮彩龙、斗龙舟，中元节兰盆会等，既是迎神赛会，又往往和集市贸易、文娱体育活动结合在一起，促进了城乡物资交流，推动了饮食文化、民间工艺美术、民间文学，并影响其风格。温州的这些器物文化，基本特点是实用、多元、细腻、多彩，这些风格，通过文化转换，影响了乡土建筑的风格。温州乡土建筑平面布置中的环境意识，实用品格；建筑立面的不追求一个主立面，各个立面都很丰富灵巧；门台的浑重绚丽；檐的门类多，尺度深，用料大，造型丰富，等等，都是温州民俗活动的需要，也是上述一系列器物文化风格的余脉。

温州民俗的核心是神祀，带有浓厚的巫文化成份。巫文化的内涵是不求儒教那一套精神道德伦理，而注重实用，一切都物质化和生活化。巫文化和多山多水的地理环境结合，孕育出温州古人"豪古崇华黜素，竞势逐利，以财力侈靡相雄长"（《古今图书集成·职方典》见李国豪主编，建筑苑拾英。上海：同济大学出版社，1998年版）、"江南之气躁动，厥（土）人性轻扬"（见唐《通典》）、"水国者，……其人灵动而知变"（见清《赌棋山庄集》）及敢于向海外拓展，"弃本争末，竞势逐利"的性格和亲近山水的文化心理图式。这些心理图式，影响了乡土建筑的风格。
sections.content_en:
4. Folk Customs and Wenzhou Vernacular Architectural Culture

"Fengsu" (customs) is an important factor influencing the type and style of residences. "Feng" refers to national customs, which influence and form the commonality of residences; "su" refers to folk customs, which create the individuality of residences.

Analyzing Chapter 1, Wenzhou folk customs have the following characteristics: ① Frequent activities — from the first month to the twelfth month, on the first or fifteenth day, on days with three, eight, two, seven, etc., there are folk activities. ② Wide scope of activities — from cities, market towns to rural areas, regardless of age, all people participate. ③ Strong gathering nature — many activities are not family-style but community and local, with everyone集中 in one place or going to one location. ④ Strong competitiveness — many folk activities are competitive, such as dragon boat racing. Some are not formally competitive but essentially have competitive elements, such as dragon lantern dancing, lantern festivals, and "flower sacrifices," with participants in units of villages, streets, or families, all having the awareness of comparing who does better. ⑤ Culturally, they carry strong shamanic cultural elements, both revering gods and entertaining oneself.

Folk activities need carriers or places; their carriers are mostly buildings, and places are mostly public land. For example, temple stage opera: the stage is temporarily built, generally chosen on public open space in the village, or threshing ground, or flat ground in front of the ancestral hall, or at the foot of a mountain, or at the intersection of several roads, by water, or at bridgeheads. The flower sacrifices (displaying bonsai, arranging flowers) in the Lanjiefu (Street-blocking Blessing) activity are mostly placed in front of doors, under eaves corridors, and some are集中 in a public building. As for divine sacrifices, most require temples and shrines to be built.

The results of folk activities, spiritually enhancing people's creativity and competitiveness, thus stimulated architectural construction activities, becoming the driving force of vernacular architecture, and influencing the style of architecture and decoration. For example, the Wenruitang River is an inland river excavated in the Tang and Song dynasties for developing polder fields. In the Ming and Qing dynasties, due to the need for sacrificial activities, people used the convenience of boats to build stages on both banks for opera performances, building more than ten temples, then called "water stages." During sacrificial activities, local opera troupes were invited to perform, while merchants gathered forming the unique "market fair," and gradually formed villages and towns. Coupled with transportation and farmland development, this formed the today's scene of market towns connected end to end before the world.

Wenzhou's divine sacrifices include sacrificing to the earth god, worshipping ancient official duties such as "Wenchang Temple" and "Medicine King Temple," sacrificing to historical figures such as Shennong, Xu Yanwang, and Wang Xizhi, and sacrificing to responsive deities such as "Zhongjing Shengwang" and "Hugong Dadi," forming the landscape characteristic of Wenzhou vernacular architecture with temples and ancestral halls everywhere. Wenzhou folk activities such as the first-month Lantern Festival dragon dance, the third-month third-day Lanjiefu, Duanwu colorful dragon and dragon boat racing, and the Zhongyuan Ullambana Festival are both welcoming-god competitions and often combined with market trade, cultural, entertainment, and sports activities, promoting urban-rural material exchange, advancing food culture, folk arts and crafts, and folk literature, and influencing their styles. These utensil cultures in Wenzhou have basic characteristics of practicality, diversity, delicacy, and colorfulness; these styles, through cultural transformation, influenced the style of vernacular architecture. The environmental awareness and practical character in the plane layout of Wenzhou vernacular architecture; the building facades not pursuing one main facade, with each facade rich and灵巧; the heavy and gorgeous gate platforms; the many types of eaves with deep scale, large materials, and rich forms — all are needs of Wenzhou folk activities and also the legacy of the above series of utensil cultural styles.

The core of Wenzhou folk customs is divine sacrifice, with strong shamanic cultural elements. The connotation of shamanic culture is not seeking the set of spiritual, moral, and ethical principles of Confucianism, but emphasizing practicality, with everything materialized and生活化. The combination of shamanic culture and the mountainous and watery geographical environment gestated the ancient Wenzhou people's character of "valuing the ancient and advocating the ornate while rejecting the plain, competing for power and profit, vying with wealth and extravagance" ("Gujin Tushu Jicheng · Zhifang Dian" in Li Guohao ed., Architectural Garden Gleanings. Shanghai: Tongji University Press, 1998 edition), "the Jiangnan air is restless, its people are light and buoyant" (see Tang "Tongdian"), "water country people... are agile and know change" (see Qing "Duqi Shanzhuang Ji"), and the character of daring to expand overseas, "abandoning the fundamental to compete for the trivial, competing for power and profit," and the cultural psychological schema of being close to mountains and waters. These psychological schemas influenced the style of vernacular architecture.

sections.name: 五、士与温州乡土建筑文化
sections.content_zh:
五、"士"与温州乡土建筑文化

传统的说法，我国古代文明都是劳动人民创造的，从客观角度讲，这个观点当然没错，但从某些具体角度看，就不能一概而论了。作者考察温州古民居良久，认为古人留给今天的乡土建筑文化，绝对不能抹杀"士"人的作用。这里所称之"士"，范围要比今人心目的知识分子广一些，它还包括那些官吏和不当官的乡贤，以及以某种知识技能为职业的人。

"士"字甲文作⊥，一像地，一像苗插入地中之形（见杨树达《积微小学述林》）。若将建筑比作树，则"士"的栽树之劳是不可埋没的。

温州是名士荟萃之地，也是出士的地方。不知是温州山水及地理位置上的特殊原因，六朝时温州郡守竟多为文坛巨星，如东晋大书法家、大学问家王羲之，刘宋时期著名诗人、赋家孙绰，中国山水诗鼻祖谢灵运，诗人骈文家、文论家颜延延，史学家裴松之、萧梁，文学家丘迟都是当时的文坛领袖，可以说这些人是当初中国文化的代表。之后的温州太守，也多为传世学士、文坛俊彦，如北宋的杨蟠、胡则，南宋的张九诚、王十朋、楼鐂、杨简，明代的何文渊、文林等。唐代诗人王维有一首诗写道："前墅树参天，千山响杜鹃。山中一夜雨，树梢百重泉。汉女输橦布，巴人讼芋田。文翁翻教授，敢不倚先贤"（《送梓州李使君》）。王维勉励友人李某向前辈学习，到一个地方任官应以"教化"民风为大任。史实确实如此，古代地方官都将"教化"当作主要职责。这些父母官，都十分尊重温州的人文传统，他们是传统文化的官员，也以礼乐教化为第一政务，为师重于为官，他们的主要任务是"助人伦，成教化"。由于他们的教化，孕育了良好的温州地方风俗。诚如《永嘉县志》转《旧志》所说："晋立郡城，生齿日烦，王右军导之以文教，谢康乐继之，乃知向方。自是家务为学，至宋逐称小邹鲁"。又说："王羲之尚滋惠，谢灵运招士讲学，由是人知向学，民风一变"。我国古代文坛领袖王羲之、谢灵运两人对温州山水的开发功不可没，唐代的杜甫《送裴虬尉永嘉》中有句：隐吏适梅福，看山忆谢公"，对他们念念不忘，清初诗人梅调元《王谢祠》诗又一再提到"前守推王谢……俯仰一含情"。

他们不仅教化民风，还提倡建筑的教化作用，建教化建筑。

在温州历史上的地方长官（郡守）中，应该特别提一下明代的温州太守文林。他是江南名士文征明的父亲，长洲人，明朝成化年间进士，当过永嘉知县，升南京太仆寺丞，又迁知温州府。该人精于堪舆、卜筮、易数，他在温州府期间，大力提倡乡规族范，促进了乡土建筑文化的繁荣。汉唐沿袭了近千年的门阀制度，到了宋代基本消失，代之而起的社会组织力量就是宗族，士人在这个变化过程中起了关键作用。当时文坛领袖范仲淹、欧阳修、苏东坡竭力提倡民间写家谱，建宗祠，设义田，目的在于抚老恤贫，保证族里的人吃、穿、嫁、娶、葬都有着落，从而稳定了社会。宋代的理学家把它发展为乡约。以吕大钧为代表，他在家乡兰田推行之后，"关中风俗为之一变"。于是"乡约"便成为理学家用心发扬礼乐教化的教课书。宋室南渡之后，朱熹在浙江福建一带推行吕氏乡约，温州各县的大宗族都在这时期形成。太守文林到温州后，强有力地抓起这个武器，在温州所属各县推行"族范"，提倡写族谱、族规、家训等，严格规范了乡民的思维方式、行为方式和价值观念。这一制度，增强了乡亲的凝聚力，族人便能联合起来，把投资方向转向公益事业，如修水利、铺路、建庙、建宗祠、建亭子等。我们今天看到的农村里布满大大小小的宗祠、亭子等，就是这一行为的物化。

温州又以山水秀丽闻名于天下，使"天下之士行过是邦者莫不俯仰留连，吟咏不辍，以诧其胜"（《光绪永嘉县志》）。如晋代著名训古学家、文学家郭璞曾客寓于温，时人请他拓卜选址、规划营建了温州古城。魏晋时代产生的玄风，温州也很流行，很多学人到山林中去寄托情怀，温州秀丽的山水吸引了不少名士，如梁时"山中宰相"陶弘景长期隐居于瑞安陶山和永嘉大若岩，对温州山水的保护与开发起了深远的影响。后来，玄风（黄老之学）和儒佛结合，不少士人和佛家子弟在深山老林中建宅第、造寺院。又如孙权、谢灵运、唐太宗、颜真卿、郭子仪、钱缪、宋太宗等大家名族的后裔，均因温州是偏安之地以及为温州山水吸引，散居于温州的溪谷竹篁之间，对温州的建筑文化，作出过积极贡献。

温州由于地形封闭，寇不能入，是避乱之地。据平阳、泰顺、瑞安、永嘉等县的宗谱记载，现存的温州好多村落，是福建大户为避战乱逃荒而来建立的。如瑞安县志记载该县的：固义、高楼、上垟、罗溪、上村、东原、后垟、陶岙、河头、杨宅、任宅、下呈、后村、李山、凤村、下林、石岗、上潘、前池、瑶庄、冯岙，以及枫岭乡、宁益乡的很多村落都是元明清各代由福建迁来的，其中就有许多士人。如史记公元933年，闽国王延钧、王延政先后称帝，互相攻杀，闽地大批仕官人家逃到温州来，建立了许多村落。如现存很多优秀古建筑的永嘉苍坡、芙蓉、溪口、枫林、花坦、廊下、岩头等楠溪江中游重要村落，就是福建长溪（今宁州）望族来落户而发展起来的。

温州的学术，晋唐间没有什么建树。自北宋周行已传播关、洛之学，学术风气开始大盛。乾隆《永嘉县志·学校》载："永嘉于宋名贤辈出，登洛闽之堂者，后先相望，郁郁彬彬，至称为小邹鲁，何其盛哉"。朱熹及其弟子们在温州办了不少书院，温州不少文人学士成了理学家。单就永嘉县说，北宋有程门弟子13人，南宋有朱门弟子16人，如溪口村的戴述、戴迅、戴溪、戴蒙、戴侗，塘湾村的郑伯熊、郑伯英、郑伯海三兄弟等，都是当时重要的理学家，并与朱熹有来往。乾隆《永嘉县志》里曾记载过这么一段佳话：朱熹曾到温州访问当地理学家，先到岩头村访问"以理学名于世"的刘愈，说："过楠溪不识刘进之，如过洞庭不认识橘"，不巧没碰上，又到谢岙访问门人谢复经，再访戴蒙、戴侗及蓬溪村李时靖。偏僻的温州和当时的文化主流保持着这样密切的联系，又达到这么高的水平，实属全国乡村少见。这些学士们提高了乡村的文化素质，为恬淡的乡土建筑做好了精神准备。

关、洛之学经南宋薛季宣、郑伯熊、陈傅良等人的批判、发展，到叶适时，终于创立了与关、洛之学相对立的事功之学，这就是我国历史上著名的永嘉学派。永嘉学派一洗理学的浮文虚论，提倡行实事，有功实，促进了社会经济和文化的繁荣，为建筑业提供了强大的经济基础，到明代乡土建筑形成高潮。

现在重点提一下南宋的"耕读"政策，宋仁宗规定，工商业者及其子女不能参加科举考试，只许于士人、农家子弟考试做官，而且规定士子必须在本乡读书应试。山清水秀的温州成为耕读社会的理想境地，逐出现了"士风侵盛……，异才辈出，往往甲于东南（宋王十朋《何提刑墓志铭》）的局面。据《温州府志》及其他有关文献记载，从北宋"天圣甲子宋郊榜"至南宋"咸淳甲戌王龙泽榜"250余年间，温州出了文科进士1300多人。仅南宋140余年间，就出文科状元5名，文科榜眼4名，文科进士1147名。这些人的背后，还有一个庞大的"士"阶层，他们世代相传，成为温州优秀传统建筑的主要投资者、营造者。

下面回过头来看看一些历史事实和发生机制。

元代，江南士人多有着眷故国之思，朝廷对士人实行笼络、优惠政策。这批士人少数服务朝庭，大多数回到家乡，过着宽裕优游、安居暇食、夸谈礼乐的隐士式生活。他们除了把玩诗书琴棋之外，构筑园林屋宇便成了一大乐趣。逐后计成的《园冶》和李渔的《闲情偶寄》问世也就在情理之中了。实践证明，学术的繁荣和相应事业的发展必是一致的。元代永嘉人王振鹏能成为我国当时最著名的"界画师"，就和家乡建筑盛况对他的感染、启发有关；反过来，他的艺术成就也必影响家乡建筑。

元末农民起义军领袖陈友谅在温州的亲戚家生活过很长一段时间。他手下的谋士多有温州人，事败后这些谋士回家乡潜心学术，对温州的建筑文化又起了推动作用。

陈友谅从温州乡村带去一批士人，明代朱元璋亦从温州乡村带去一批士人。朱元璋的高参刘伯温是温州人，起义成功后他却弃官回故里，传播光大了乡村文化。再说朱元璋对知识分子实行容忍政策，能让他们在农村生存光大。经过这些重大的历史事件和几代积蓄，到明代，温州乡间"士人"成了乡村社会的领导阶层。明代嘉靖、隆庆时期出现了稍安局面，万历初年实行"一条鞭"法，人民生活安定，社会经济繁荣，出现"四海升平"现象。这以后，土地兼并加剧、财富集中，资本主义萌芽，国家出现了徽商、苏商、晋商，他们掀起了造园热潮，文化艺术更加繁荣。造园家张涟、张南阳应世，计成的《园冶》问世，李渔的《闲情偶寄》诞生，温州民间曲艺盛行，这些自然影响住宅建设，使住宅建设掀起了热潮。这些士人既是乡村精神的领导者，也是乡村建设的领导者，他们的主要作用是倡导、捐资组织乡村建设，并把他们的山水情怀和审美观念渗透到建筑物和乡村风貌中。因此，可以说，我们今天看到的温州乡土建筑那种朴素恬淡的风格就是那些士人们的风格。

作者看过永嘉岩头、苍坡、芙蓉、渠口、塘湾族谱，调查过这些村及坦下、棣头、泰顺雪溪、三魁、乐清南阁等古村落一些"大屋"古宅，认为主要是"士"作用的结果。如苍坡村，堪称温州地方传统民居的宝库。据《李氏宗谱》记载："登科及第列士版者代不泛人，此皆由于诗书一脉起家"。又如芙蓉村现存的"书院"、"老屋"、"明宅"等五座，源盖于该村宋代"耕读"之风抚育下，"科名甲第，雀起蝉联，文武簪缨，云蒸霞蔚"（见芙蓉《陈氏家谱》）。又据《永嘉鹤阳谢氏宗谱》记载，该村为谢灵运家族繁衍，第十一始祖裕孙公（公元1311—1375年）殖业繁藩，创弟宏敞。同是该村，明代出了个受五朝皇帝宠遇的宫庭画师谢延循（公元1377—1452年），曾封为锦衣卫千户，在家乡建了一所静乐轩和水亭，士大夫与之游者皆赋诗，连宣宗皇帝也为此亭赠诗："暮色动前轩，重城欲闭门。残霞收赤气，新月破黄昏。已觉乾坤静，都无市井喧，阴阳有恒理，斯与达人论。"

永嘉豫章村有一门三代五进士之说。明代中书舍人胡宗韫（谢延循的朋友）告老归田，在故宅"中翰第"造了一座紫薇楼以为养闲之所。

永嘉《棠川郑氏宗谱》记乡绅郑公谔回故里"筑美室，置图书"，常与朋友"啸傲于烟霞泉石间"（棠川即塘湾）。

明代晚期，永嘉塘湾村的乡贤郑世益虽然没有外出经商，但他精于理财，"铢积寸累，握算持筹，不数年而陈粟贯朽，富甲一邑，居屋肆宏莫比。"

永嘉《蓬溪谢氏宗谱》记：谢朗离乡营商数十年，厌恶城市喧闹，归耕田里，"筑室创业，富望一乡"。

永嘉《蓬溪谢氏宗谱》记：北宋咸淳乙酉进士李靖回造了一条石板整齐的街（后人称为状元街），现存的李靖古宅规模十分宏大，有西屋七间，深9.5m，有前廊檐，深1.5m，两厢三间，设有檐廊，进深8m，房屋四面全是木板壁木装修，直棂窗，用料粗拙，柱子不高，下用木础，也有地砖。

永嘉蓬溪明代水院大宅是章纶（明朝礼部尚书）的表兄弟所建，房屋占地面阔13开间（45～50m）深39m，三进两院，后面的小院为水池，左右有小天井，形成日月井格局，两旁还有附加房间，总间数不下50间。蓬溪近云山舍，是清代邑庠生谢文波所建，他在同治五年到苏州遍访名宅大第，回乡建造了这座四合院。院落遍宽，用两道花雕砖墙分隔为三部分，该砖墙现为县级文保单位。大门上"近云山舍"四字出于朱熹，左边厢房名"听香斋"是清代翁同酥书额。岩头村南宋初建村，明代嘉靖年间开始大发展，主要得力于两个人：一位是进士金昭，现存的岩头大宗祠、上花园、下花园、进士牌楼是金昭或纪念金昭的作品。另一位乡贤桂林公"屡试不中，转而青囊，相宅卜地"，"资利之多，功德之盛，应推府君第一"。现在人们看到的丽水湖、丽水街、塔湖庙、接官亭以及已毁的文峰塔、书斋森秀轩、汤山书院都是他规划建造的。岩头村几条主要街巷（进士街、横街、浚水街、中央街）两旁的一批三井两院大宅，也是桂林公的杰作，其规划严整，气魄宏大，令今人看了赞叹不绝。

永嘉水云村山顶现存最古朴的古宅是清代咸丰年间贡生陈福建造，有浙江巡抚罗某的题匾"登崇俊良选"。

永嘉溪口村东山书院，是南宋进士、著名理学家戴蒙辞官之后创办的。

永嘉埭头村现存古宅很多，则是另一类型宅的创作者。这个村在清代是温州建筑业的专业村，这些有技艺的人，可称为准文人学士，他们外出创业，挣了钱后回家乡施展自己的技艺和经济实力，门楼、花墙、亭阁争艳斗丽，今存鲁班祠，是这段历史的写照。

泰顺雪溪石门楼（照14-3），是我国近代数学家胡维基的故居，正屋是其祖父胡东伟所建（公元1833年），两侧厢房建于道光二十一年（公元1842年），下堂南北及前堂建于咸丰二年（公元1833年），石门楼的建筑史，可以追溯到胡的曾祖胡朝桂，官封奉直大夫，其下为祖父胡东伟，官封奉直大夫（世袭），生六子，长子为贡生，二子、三子为大学士，四子得杰为直隶州州判，五子得栖为邑庠生，六子得庶为大学士。

另外，如泰顺三魁镇下武洋林家厝，三魁镇"七榴"张宅，三魁镇"九榴"张宅，泰顺县里光林宅、陈宅、徐岙吴宅，新浦夏宅等等，都是名门望族、士人留下的作品。

"士"对建筑的影响还在于它的题词成了建筑的相辅相成部分，起到了寓教化于建筑的作用。如永嘉蓬溪古村落谢宅，朱熹的题词"近云山舍"、"忠孝持家远、诗书处世长"等，开拓了房屋意境。平阳青街林宅门联"当户青山延秀色，环门绿水起文波"激起人们求学之思。

可以说，我们现在看到的古代乡土优秀民居，大部分是"士"所造。这些故居，既是他们精心运思的作品，又是他们恬淡安然、耕读传家的生活舞台，从现存的这些古居中，我们犹可追寻这些在乡下高品位文人贤士们的文化心理和价值取向。为使读者能细细品悟其中之三味，现摘录一段当时乡村士大夫营建宅第的兴致和生活：

"彦通（永乐间人）纯实谨愿，不为簿习。遇高人硕士，辄倾于觞酒间。乃度其所居堂之后，爽垲幽间，宜楼居，乃构楼若干楹，楼之左右宜竹，又而植以竹也。重檐峻出，四窗虚敞，而朝云暮雨，散旭敷晴，则荫连溪碧，翠接山寒。夫楼中之佳致也，多在于竹。彦通每于风朝月夜，携朋挈侣，施施然游息于斯楼之上以极其萧洒者，盖其襟度宏深，神情超畅，能不以天地间事物为心虑也"。这一段话活脱脱地记述了当年乡士们的精神追求和生活方式，这里面流露出来的那种细腻的、与自然微妙结合的生活神韵，也正是温州乡土民居的韵味。

5. "Shi" (Scholar-Officials) and Wenzhou Vernacular Architectural Culture

The traditional view is that ancient Chinese civilization was all created by the working people. From an objective perspective, this view is of course correct, but from certain specific angles, it cannot be generalized. The author has investigated Wenzhou's ancient residences for a long time and believes that the vernacular architectural culture left by ancient people to today absolutely cannot erase the role of "shi" (scholar-officials). The "shi" referred to here has a broader scope than today's intellectuals; it also includes those officials and non-official village worthies, as well as people who make a living from certain knowledge and skills.

The character "shi" in oracle bone script is written as ⊥, one stroke resembling earth, one resembling a seedling inserted into the earth (see Yang Shuda, "Jiwei Xiaoxue Shulin"). If architecture is compared to a tree, then the "shi's" tree-planting labor cannot be buried.

Wenzhou is a place where famous scholars gather, and also a place that produces scholars. Whether due to Wenzhou's landscapes and special geographical location, during the Six Dynasties period Wenzhou's prefects were unexpectedly mostly literary giants, such as the Eastern Jin great calligrapher and scholar Wang Xizhi, the Liu Song period famous poet and rhapsodist Sun Chuo, the founder of Chinese landscape poetry Xie Lingyun, the poet, parallel prose writer, and literary theorist Yan Yanzhi, the historians Pei Songzhi and Xiao Liang, and the writer Qiu Chi — all were literary leaders of the time, and it can be said these people were representatives of Chinese culture at that time. Later Wenzhou prefects were also mostly传世 scholars and literary talents, such as the Northern Song's Yang Pan and Hu Ze, the Southern Song's Zhang Jiucheng, Wang Shipeng, Lou Yue, and Yang Jian, and the Ming's He Wenyuan and Wen Lin. The Tang poet Wang Wei wrote a poem: "The front villa has towering trees, a thousand mountains echo with cuckoos. A night of rain in the mountains, treetops have a hundred layers of springs. Han women pay tong cloth, Ba people dispute taro fields. Wen Weng turned to teaching, dare not rely on former sages" ("Sending Prefect Li of Zizhou"). Wang Wei encouraged his friend Li to learn from predecessors and take "educating" local customs as a major responsibility when serving as an official. Historical facts are indeed so; ancient local officials all regarded "education" as their main duty. These parent officials highly respected Wenzhou's humanistic tradition; they were officials of traditional culture and also took ritual and music education as their first political duty, with teaching more important than officialdom, their main task being "to help human relations, achieve education." Due to their education, good Wenzhou local customs were gestated. As the "Yongjia County Annals" quoting the "Old Annals" says: "When the commandery city was established in Jin, population grew daily; Wang Youjun (Wang Xizhi) guided with culture and education, Xie Kangle (Xie Lingyun) continued, and people knew the right direction. From then on families devoted to learning, and by the Song dynasty it was called 'little Zou-Lu'." It also says: "Wang Xizhi still spread benevolence, Xie Lingyun recruited scholars to lecture, hence people knew to study, and local customs changed." The ancient Chinese literary leaders Wang Xizhi and Xie Lingyun made indelible contributions to the development of Wenzhou's landscapes. The Tang poet Du Fu's "Sending Pei Qiu as Wei of Yongjia" has the line: "The recluse official meets Mei Fu, viewing mountains recalls Xie Gong" — never forgetting them. The early Qing poet Mei Tiaoyuan's poem "Wang-Xie Shrine" repeatedly mentions "former prefects Wang and Xie... looking up and down with emotion."

They not only educated local customs but also advocated the educational function of architecture, building educational architecture.

Among Wenzhou's historical local officials (prefects), special mention should be made of the Ming dynasty Wenzhou prefect Wen Lin. He was the father of the Jiangnan famous scholar Wen Zhengming, a native of Changzhou, a Jinshi of the Ming Chenghua period, who served as County Magistrate of Yongjia, was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud in Nanjing, and later became Prefect of Wenzhou. This person was skilled in feng shui, divination, and I Ching numerology. During his tenure in Wenzhou, he vigorously promoted village rules and clan norms, promoting the prosperity of vernacular architectural culture. The clan system inherited for nearly a thousand years from Han and Tang dynasties basically disappeared by the Song dynasty, replaced by clan organization as the social force, and scholars played a key role in this change process. At that time, literary leaders Fan Zhongyan, Ouyang Xiu, and Su Dongpo vigorously advocated folk genealogy writing, ancestral hall building, and charitable land establishment, aiming to care for the elderly and relieve the poor, ensuring that clan members had food, clothing, marriage, and burial, thus stabilizing society. Song dynasty Neo-Confucians developed this into village covenants (xiangyue). Represented by Lü Dajun, after he implemented it in his hometown Lantian, "Guanzhong customs changed completely." Thus "village covenants" became textbooks for Neo-Confucians to diligently promote ritual and music education. After the Song court moved south, Zhu Xi promoted the Lü family village covenant in Zhejiang and Fujian, and the major clans in various Wenzhou counties all formed during this period. After Prefect Wen Lin arrived in Wenzhou, he powerfully took up this weapon, promoting "clan norms" in all counties under Wenzhou, advocating writing genealogies, clan rules, and family instructions, strictly standardizing villagers' thinking, behavior, and values. This system enhanced the cohesion of villagers, enabling clan members to unite and redirect investment toward public welfare, such as building water conservancy, paving roads, building temples, ancestral halls, and pavilions. The large and small ancestral halls and pavilions we see in rural areas today are the materialization of this behavior.

Wenzhou is also famous worldwide for its beautiful landscapes, making "scholars passing through this state all look up and down, lingering, chanting endlessly, to marvel at its beauty" ("Guangxu Yongjia County Annals"). For example, the Jin dynasty famous phonologist and writer Guo Pu once resided in Wenzhou; locals asked him to divine site selection and plan and build the ancient Wenzhou city. The Xuan (mysterious) style generated in the Wei-Jin period was also popular in Wenzhou, with many scholars going to mountains and forests to entrust their feelings. Wenzhou's beautiful landscapes attracted many famous scholars; for example, the Liang dynasty "mountain prime minister" Tao Hongjing long lived in seclusion in Taoshan, Rui'an and Daruoyan, Yongjia, having a profound influence on the protection and development of Wenzhou's landscapes. Later, the Xuan style (Huang-Lao thought) combined with Confucianism and Buddhism, and many scholars and Buddhist disciples built residences and temples in deep mountains and old forests. Also, descendants of famous families such as Sun Quan, Xie Lingyun, Emperor Taizong of Tang, Yan Zhenqing, Guo Ziyi, Qian Liu, and Emperor Taizong of Song all scattered in Wenzhou's valleys and bamboo groves because Wenzhou was a safe haven and attracted by its landscapes, making positive contributions to Wenzhou's architectural culture.

Due to its enclosed terrain, Wenzhou could not be invaded by bandits, making it a refuge from chaos. According to genealogies of Pingyang, Taishun, Rui'an, and Yongjia counties, many existing Wenzhou villages were established by major Fujian families fleeing war and famine. For example, the Rui'an County Annals record that villages in the county such as Guyi, Gaolou, Shangyang, Luoxi, Shangcun, Dongyuan, Houyang, Tao'ao, Hetou, Yangzhai, Renzhai, Xiacheng, Houcun, Lishan, Fengcun, Xialin, Shigang, Shangpan, Qianchi, Yaozhuang, Feng'ao, as well as many villages in Fengling Township and Ningyi Township, were all migrated from Fujian during the Yuan, Ming, and Qing dynasties, among whom there were many scholars. For example, historical records show that in 933 AD, Min kings Wang Yanjun and Wang Yanzheng successively proclaimed themselves emperors and attacked each other, causing大批 official families from Min to flee to Wenzhou and establish many villages. For example, the important middle-Nanxi River villages with many excellent ancient buildings — Cangpo, Furong, Xikou, Fenglin, Huatan, Langxia, and Yantou in Yongjia — were developed by prominent families from Changxi (now Ningzhou), Fujian who settled there.

Wenzhou's scholarship had no achievements during the Jin and Tang periods. Since the Northern Song Zhou Xingyi propagated Guan and Luo learning, the academic atmosphere began to flourish. Qianlong's "Yongjia County Annals · Schools" records: "Yongjia in the Song dynasty had famous sages emerging in succession, those entering the halls of Luo and Min learning followed one after another, cultured and refined, even called 'little Zou-Lu,' how prosperous!" Zhu Xi and his disciples established many academies in Wenzhou, and many Wenzhou literati and scholars became Neo-Confucians. In Yongjia County alone, the Northern Song had 13 disciples of the Cheng school, and the Southern Song had 16 disciples of the Zhu school; for example, the Dai family of Xikou Village — Dai Shu, Dai Xun, Dai Xi, Dai Meng, Dai Dong — and the Zheng brothers of Tangwan Village — Zheng Boxiong, Zheng Boying, Zheng Bohai — were all important Neo-Confucians of the time and had contacts with Zhu Xi. Qianlong's "Yongjia County Annals" recorded such a charming story: Zhu Xi once visited Wenzhou to meet local Neo-Confucians. He first went to Yantou Village to visit Liu Yu, "famous for Neo-Confucianism in the world," saying: "Passing Nanxi without knowing Liu Jinzhi is like passing Dongting without knowing oranges." Unfortunately he didn't meet him, then went to Xie'ao to visit disciple Xie Fujing, then visited Dai Meng, Dai Dong, and Li Shijing of Pengxi Village. The remote Wenzhou maintained such close contact with the cultural mainstream of the time and reached such a high level, truly rare in rural areas nationwide. These scholars improved the cultural quality of the countryside and made spiritual preparations for the tranquil vernacular architecture.

Guan and Luo learning, through the critique and development of Southern Song Xue Jixuan, Zheng Boxiong, and Chen Fuliang, finally by Ye Shi established the utilitarian learning opposing Guan and Luo learning — this is the famous Yongjia School in Chinese history. The Yongjia School washed away the empty rhetoric of Neo-Confucianism, advocating practical deeds and real achievements, promoting the prosperity of social economy and culture, providing a strong economic foundation for the construction industry, and by the Ming dynasty vernacular architecture reached a climax.

Now focusing on the Southern Song "farming-studying" (gengdu) policy: Emperor Renzong of Song stipulated that merchants, artisans, and their children could not take the imperial examination, only scholars and farmers' children could take exams to become officials, and stipulated that scholars must study and take exams in their hometown. The picturesque Wenzhou became an ideal place for farming-studying society, gradually出现了 "scholarship prevailing... outstanding talents emerging, often leading the southeast" (Song Wang Shipeng, "Epitaph of He Tixing"). According to "Wenzhou Prefecture Annals" and other relevant documents, from the Northern Song "Tiansheng Jiazi Song Jiao ranking" to the Southern Song "Xianchun Jiaxu Wang Longze ranking" over 250 years, Wenzhou produced over 1300 literary jinshi. In just the 140+ years of the Southern Song, it produced 5 literary zhuangyuan (top scholars), 4 literary bangyan (second-place scholars), and 1147 literary jinshi. Behind these people was also a庞大 "shi" stratum, passed down through generations, becoming the main investors and builders of Wenzhou's excellent traditional architecture.

Now let's look back at some historical facts and mechanisms.

In the Yuan dynasty, Jiangnan scholars mostly had thoughts of眷 the former country, and the court implemented笼络 and preferential policies toward scholars. A minority of these scholars served the court, while most returned to their hometowns, living a hermit-style life of comfort, leisure, and discussing ritual and music. Besides appreciating poetry, calligraphy, and chess, building gardens and houses became a great pleasure. Subsequently, the publication of Ji Cheng's "Yuan Ye" (Garden Treatise) and Li Yu's "Xian Qing Ou Ji" (Casual Notes on Idle Feelings) was only natural. Practice proves that academic prosperity and corresponding career development must be consistent. The Yuan dynasty Yongjia native Wang Zhenpeng becoming the most famous "jiehua" (ruled-line painting) painter in China at that time was related to the influence and inspiration of his hometown's architectural prosperity; conversely, his artistic achievements must also have influenced his hometown's architecture.

The late Yuan peasant rebel leader Chen Youliang lived for a long time at a relative's home in Wenzhou. Many of his advisors were Wenzhou people; after his defeat, these advisors returned to their hometowns to devote themselves to scholarship, further promoting Wenzhou's architectural culture.

Chen Youliang took a group of scholars from Wenzhou's countryside, and the Ming dynasty Zhu Yuanzhang also took a group of scholars from Wenzhou's countryside. Zhu Yuanzhang's senior advisor Liu Bowen was a Wenzhou native; after the uprising succeeded, he resigned and returned to his hometown, spreading and enhancing rural culture. Moreover, Zhu Yuanzhang implemented a tolerant policy toward intellectuals, allowing them to survive and flourish in the countryside. Through these major historical events and several generations of accumulation, by the Ming dynasty, Wenzhou's rural "scholars" became the leading stratum of rural society. During the Ming Jiajing and Longqing periods, a relatively stable situation emerged; in the early Wanli period, the "single whip" tax law was implemented, people's lives were stable, social economy prospered, and a "world peace" phenomenon appeared. After this, land annexation intensified, wealth concentrated, capitalism萌芽, and the country saw Huizhou merchants, Suzhou merchants, and Shanxi merchants, who掀起 a garden-building craze, with culture and art more prosperous. Garden builders Zhang Lian and Zhang Nanyang appeared, Ji Cheng's "Yuan Ye" was published, Li Yu's "Xian Qing Ou Ji" was born, and Wenzhou folk performing arts flourished — these naturally influenced residential construction,掀起 a热潮 in residential building. These scholars were both leaders of rural spirit and leaders of rural construction; their main role was to advocate, donate, and organize rural construction, and渗透 their landscape sentiments and aesthetic concepts into buildings and rural landscapes. Therefore, it can be said that the simple and tranquil style of Wenzhou vernacular architecture we see today is the style of those scholars.

The author has read genealogies of Yantou, Cangpo, Furong, Qukou, and Tangwan in Yongjia, and investigated "big house" ancient residences in these villages and in Tanxia, Ditou, Xuexi and Sankui in Taishun, and Nange in Yueqing, believing they are mainly the result of "shi" influence. For example, Cangpo Village can be called a treasure house of Wenzhou local traditional residences. According to the "Li Family Genealogy": "Those passing the imperial examination and listed as scholars were not rare in each generation, all due to the poetry and books tradition starting the family." Another example is the five existing buildings in Furong Village — "Academy," "Old House," "Ming Residence," etc. — all originating from the village's Song dynasty "farming-studying" ethos, with "imperial examination success rising continuously, civil and military officials flourishing" (see Furong "Chen Family Genealogy"). Also according to the "Yongjia Heyang Xie Family Genealogy," this village was where the Xie Lingyun family multiplied; the 11th ancestor Yusun Gong (1311-1375 AD) prospered in business and built spacious residences. In the same village, the Ming dynasty produced a court painter Xie Yanxun (1377-1452 AD) favored by five emperors, who was appointed as a battalion commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, and built a Jingle Pavilion and Water Pavilion in his hometown; scholar-officials who visited him all wrote poems, and even the Xuande Emperor wrote a poem for this pavilion: "Twilight moves before the pavilion, the heavy city is about to close its gates. Remaining sunset gathers red qi, new moon breaks through dusk. Already feeling heaven and earth quiet, no market noise at all, yin and yang have constant principles, this is discussed with the enlightened."

Yongjia Yuzhang Village has the saying of three generations and five jinshi in one family. The Ming dynasty Zhongshu Sheren (Palace Secretary) Hu Zongyun (friend of Xie Yanxun) retired to his hometown and built a Ziwei Tower in his former residence "Zhonghan Di" as a place for leisure.

Yongjia "Tangchuan Zheng Family Genealogy" records that local gentleman Zheng Gong'e returned to his hometown "built a beautiful house, placed books," often with friends "roaming among mist, clouds, springs, and rocks" (Tangchuan is Tangwan).

In the late Ming dynasty, the Yongjia Tangwan Village worthy Zheng Shiyi did not go out to do business, but he was skilled in finance, "accumulating bit by bit, calculating carefully, in a few years had stored grain and rotted strings of cash, richest in the county, with magnificent residences unmatched."

Yongjia "Pengxi Xie Family Genealogy" records: Xie Lang left home to do business for decades, disgusted with city noise, returned to farming, "built a house and started a business, wealthy and renowned in the township."

Yongjia "Pengxi Xie Family Genealogy" records: Northern Song Xianchun Yiyou jinshi Li Jing returned and built a street with neat stone slabs (later called Zhuangyuan Street). The existing Li Jing ancient residence is very grand, with seven west rooms, 9.5m deep, with front eaves corridor 1.5m deep, three-bay two wings with eaves corridors 8m deep, the house四面 all wooden board walls and wood finishing, straight-bar lattice windows, with rough materials, not-tall columns, wooden bases below, and also floor tiles.

The Yongjia Pengxi Ming dynasty Water Courtyard Mansion was built by the cousin of Zhang Lun (Ming dynasty Minister of Rites). The house occupies a width of 13 bays (45-50m) and depth of 39m, with three halls and two courtyards; the rear small courtyard is a pool, with small sky wells on left and right, forming a sun-moon well pattern, with additional rooms on both sides, total no fewer than 50 rooms. Pengxi Jinyun Shan She was built by Qing dynasty county student Xie Wenbo; in the fifth year of Tongzhi he traveled to Suzhou to visit famous residences, returning to build this quadrangle. The courtyard is wide, divided into three parts by two carved brick walls, which are now county-level cultural protection units. The four characters "Jinyun Shan She" on the gate are from Zhu Xi; the left wing room named "Tingxiang Zhai" has a plaque by Qing dynasty Weng Tongsu. Yantou Village was founded in the early Southern Song and began major development in the Ming Jiajing period, mainly due to two people: one was jinshi Jin Zhao; the existing Yantou major ancestral hall, upper garden, lower garden, and jinshi archway are works by or commemorating Jin Zhao. The other worthy Guilin Gong "repeatedly failed exams, turned to feng shui, site selection and house divination," "with much wealth and merit, should be ranked first." The Lishui Lake, Lishui Street, Tahu Temple, Jieguan Pavilion, and the destroyed Wenfeng Pagoda, Shuzhai Senxiu Xuan, and Tangshan Academy we see today were all planned and built by him. A batch of three-well two-courtyard large residences on both sides of Yantou Village's main streets (Jinshi Street, Heng Street, Junshui Street, Central Street) are also masterpieces of Guilin Gong, with rigorous planning and grand momentum, making modern viewers sigh in admiration.

The most ancient existing residence on the mountaintop of Yongjia Shuiyun Village was built by Qing dynasty Xianfeng gongsheng (tribute student) Chen Fu, with a plaque by Zhejiang Governor Luo "Deng Chong Jun Liang Xuan" (Selecting Outstanding Talents).

The Dongshan Academy in Yongjia Xikou Village was founded after the Southern Song jinshi and famous Neo-Confucian Dai Meng resigned from office.

Yongjia Daitou Village has many existing ancient residences, being creators of another type of residence. This village was a professional village of the Wenzhou construction industry in the Qing dynasty; these skilled people can be called quasi-literati scholars. They went out to start businesses, and after earning money returned to their hometown to施展 their skills and economic strength; gate towers, flower walls, and pavilions competed in beauty. The existing Luban Shrine (Carpenter God Shrine) is a portrayal of this history.

The Shimenlou in Xuexi, Taishun (photo 14-3), is the former residence of China's modern mathematician Hu Weiji. The main house was built by his grandfather Hu Dongwei (1833 AD), the two side wings were built in the 21st year of Daoguang (1842 AD), and the lower hall's north-south and front hall were built in the 2nd year of Xianfeng (1833 AD). The architectural history of Shimenlou can be traced to Hu's great-grandfather Hu Chaogui, appointed as Fengzhi Dafu (a rank), below him was grandfather Hu Dongwei, also appointed Fengzhi Dafu (hereditary), who had six sons: the eldest was a gongsheng, the second and third were dazhangshi (university students), the fourth Dejie was a prefecture judge, the fifth Deqi was a county student, and the sixth Deshu was a dazhangshi.

Additionally, such as the Lin family residence in Xiawuyang, Sankui Town, Taishun; the "Qiliu" Zhang residence in Sankui Town; the "Jiuliu" Zhang residence in Sankui Town; the Li Guanglin residence, Chen residence, Xu'ao Wu residence, and Xinpu Xia residence in Taishun County — all are works left by prominent families and scholars.

The influence of "shi" on architecture also lies in their inscriptions becoming complementary parts of architecture, playing the role of integrating education into architecture. For example, in the Xie residence of the ancient Pengxi Village in Yongjia, Zhu Xi's inscriptions "Jinyun Shan She" and "Loyalty and filial piety sustain the family far, poetry and books handle the world long" expanded the artistic conception of the house. The Pingyang Qingjie Lin residence gate couplet "Green mountains before the door extend elegant colors, green waters around the gate raise literary waves" inspired people's desire for learning.

It can be said that most of the excellent ancient vernacular residences we see today were built by "shi." These former residences are both their carefully conceived works and their tranquil, peaceful, farming-studying family tradition life stages. From these existing ancient residences, we can still trace the cultural psychology and value orientation of these high-taste literati and worthies in the countryside. To enable readers to细细 savor the essence, here is an excerpt of the enthusiasm and life of rural scholar-officials building residences at that time:

"Yantong (Yongle period person) was pure and honest, not fond of trivial habits. When meeting eminent scholars, he would pour wine with them. Then measuring behind his residence hall, a bright, high, and secluded place suitable for a building, he built several bays of building; suitable for bamboo on both sides of the building, he planted bamboo. Double eaves project high, four windows are open and spacious; with morning clouds and evening rain, scattered sunlight and clear skies, the shade connects to stream green, emerald reaches mountain cold. The fine charm of the building lies mostly in bamboo. Yantong, every windy morning and moonlit night, would bring friends and companions, leisurely resting and roaming on this building to the utmost of his elegance, because his mind was broad and deep, his spirit transcended and free, able to not let worldly things occupy his thoughts." This passage vividly records the spiritual pursuit and lifestyle of rural scholars at that time; the delicate life charm subtly combined with nature revealed here is precisely the charm of Wenzhou vernacular residences.

sections.name: 六、结语
sections.content_zh:
六、结语

以上五点，仅仅是影响温州乡土建筑文化的众多因素之一。著名建筑学家拉普普在《住屋形式与文化》中指出："住屋的形式，并不是最广义的社会因素系统的单纯结果，而是最广义的社会因素系统的共同结果"。温州的语言快捷温柔，它保持了较多唐朝以前的语法和称呼；温州的文艺门类多、节奏柔缓宛转、抒情性强；温州的地方戏（瓯剧）博采众长，曲牌多，调门低；温州的传统工艺品四雕一绣（黄杨木雕、青田石雕、彩石镶嵌、瓯塑、瓯绣）画面多彩、层次清晰；温州的菜肴讲究菜的原汁原味，都和温州的乡土建筑文化有相似之处，这些都是温州乡土建筑文化的基因。
sections.content_en:
6. Conclusion

The above five points are merely one of the many factors influencing Wenzhou's vernacular architectural culture. The famous architectural scholar Rapoport pointed out in "House Form and Culture": "The form of a house is not the simple result of the broadest social factor system, but the joint result of the broadest social factor system." Wenzhou's language is quick and gentle, retaining much grammar and terminology from before the Tang dynasty; Wenzhou's literary and artistic categories are many, with soft and graceful rhythms and strong lyricism; Wenzhou's local opera (Ou opera) absorbs many strengths, with many qupai (tune patterns) and low tonal ranges; Wenzhou's traditional crafts — four carvings and one embroidery (boxwood carving, Qingtian stone carving, colored stone inlay, Ou sculpture, Ou embroidery) — have colorful images and clear layers; Wenzhou's cuisine emphasizes the original flavor of dishes — all have similarities with Wenzhou's vernacular architectural culture, and these are all the genes of Wenzhou's vernacular architectural culture.

Part Two consists of architectural survey drawings and photographs, approximately 84 pages (page_046-129), including the following main content:

I. Architectural Survey Drawings (Figure 1-1 to 14-x)
1. Ye Clan Ancestral Hall, Qukou, Yongjia (Figures 1-1 to 1-3): front elevation, side elevation, sections (2-2 section, 3-3 section)
2. Kangle Gong Ancestral Hall, Pengxi, Yongjia (Figure 2-1): site plan, perspective view
3. Other survey drawings of ancestral halls, residences, pavilions, and covered bridges, including plans, elevations, sections, and detail drawings

1. Village environment and site selection photos (Photos 1-3, 1-7, 1-10, etc.)
2. Eaves and gable wall photos (Photos 2-1 to 2-23): various eave forms, gable walls, roof corners
3. Horizontal development and open-transparent photos (Photos 3-1 to 3-5)

6. Entrance treatment photos (Photos 7-1 to 7-19)
